items.title: Dynamical Decoupling of Nonclassical States in a Biased-Noise Spin Qudit
items.summary: Encoding quantum information in $d$-dimensional systems (qudits) with $d>2$ offers appealing new directions for resource-efficient quantum computing. However, protecting the coherence of nonclassical qudit resource states remains an open challenge. Dynamical decoupling (DD) is a well-established technique for extending coherence, but its application to qudits is hindered by the quadratic scaling of the decoupling sequence overhead with the dimension $d$. As a result, demonstrations of qudit DD have so far been limited to low-dimensional qudits. Here, we show that noise-biased qudits enable a nontrivial reduction of this overhead, for example, from quadratic to linear. We perform qudit DD on a model $d=8$ qudit, the nuclear spin of an antimony donor in silicon. We benchmark DD performance on highly nonclassical states such as uniform superpositions, cat states, and Haar random states and measure coherence improvements up to a factor $5$ to $10$. For a spin-cat error correction code, continuous DD extends the coherence time of the logical superposition $|+\rangle_L$ to $225$~ms, compared to $19$~ms under free evolution and $85$~ms with a Hahn echo. This improvement shows that DD sequences tailored to a system's noise bias can significantly enhance the lifetime of encoded logical qubits.

items.title: Active Sculpting: morphodynamics of internally stirred active vesicles
items.summary: Active flows are often confined by soft, deformable boundaries that they can push against, reshape, and in turn get reorganized by. Motivated by this interplay, we combine theory and numerical simulations to analyze the morphodynamics of an elastic vesicle enclosing a dilute suspension of extensile active particles. We model the two-dimensional vesicle as a weakly extensible elastic ring with bending rigidity, immersed in a Stokesian fluid, and describe the confined active suspension using a kinetic theory. The vesicle and the suspension are coupled hydrodynamically, through the kinematic and dynamic boundary conditions at the interface, and energetically, through a single alignment interaction that simultaneously aligns active particles with the membrane and the membrane with the particles. We show that this interaction reduces to a weak-anchoring boundary condition familiar from passive liquid crystals and derive a closed-form quiescent equilibrium state in which the nematic order in the suspension organizes into a vortex with a +1 defect core. A stability analysis of this state predicts an ordered hierarchy of activity thresholds at which successive shape modes of the vesicle are destabilized, as well as a purely passive, anchoring-driven instability of floppy vesicles. Nonlinear simulations, performed with a volume-conserving immersed boundary method, reveal that each threshold crossing gives rise to a distinct emergent state: a static spindle with boundary-pinned defects, a rotor that tank treads against its own rotation, a fluctuating spinner, and a turbulent state in which the vesicle acts as a self-stirring compartment. Beyond demonstrating how boundary deformability sculpts, and is sculpted by, confined active matter, our results open the door to study hydrodynamic interactions between such active vesicles and to use membrane fluctuations as a probe of activity of suspensions.

items.title: Neural-Network Solutions to Real-Space Charge Density and Generalization
items.summary: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem establishes that, in principle, the ground state (GS) charge density contains all GS information of a many-electron system, such that all GS observables can be expressed as functionals of the GS charge density. Conventional Kohn-Sham density functional theory requires iterative solution of the self-consistent-field equations at substantial computational cost, motivating the development of deep learning surrogates for electronic structure calculations and, in turn, accelerating computer-aided materials design. Here, we propose AIDEN, an Atomic-Interaction Density Equivariant Network for solving real-space charge density. AIDEN separates the element-dependent one-center density from environment-induced density redistribution and represents the latter through complementary atom- and edge-centered tensor correlations. A continuous low-rank Gaussian decoder then reconstructs the density at arbitrary spatial coordinates while reusing atomic encodings independently of the evaluation grid. AIDEN achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on periodic crystal benchmarks while remaining competitive for molecular systems, and further demonstrates zero-shot transferability across several structurally distinct out-of-distribution case studies. Furthermore, AIDEN provides substantially faster inference than both baseline models and full SCF calculations, enabling efficient charge density reconstruction for large-scale electronic structure calculations.

items.title: Emergent medium-range order in amorphous silicon
items.summary: Medium-range order (MRO) is an important feature of amorphous materials, but its nature in terms of atomic arrangement has remained elusive. Here, using large-scale machine-learning-driven atomistic simulations of amorphous silicon, we probe the MRO of this archetypal network glass. By characterizing the structure in three dimensions, we reveal that the symmetry of the atomic arrangement around a central atom shows a crossover as a function of distance. At short distances, the structure is determined by local bonding constraints, which evolve from predominantly tetrahedral environments in low-density amorphous silicon to highly coordinated and strongly disordered local environments in very-high-density amorphous silicon. At larger distances, however, distinct cubic- and octahedral-symmetry patterns emerge in the three-dimensional atomic-density distribution, despite the absence of these symmetries at shorter length scales. We find that this crossover is accompanied by a quasi-periodic spatial organization of the topological rings in the structure. The characteristic spacing between ring centers matches the length scale of the first sharp diffraction peak (FSDP) in the structure factor, establishing a direct connection between this reciprocal-space signature of MRO and its real-space organization. These results demonstrate that the FSDP, the spatial correlation of the rings, and emergent orientational symmetries are not independent manifestations of MRO, but reflect different aspects of a common structural organization. Our findings provide a unified real-space picture of MRO in amorphous silicon and suggest that intermediate-range structural order in network glasses emerges from the interplay between local bonding constraints and extended atomic arrangements driven by efficient packing.

items.title: Correlation-driven enhancement of pairing in a nematic Hund's metal
items.summary: Superconductivity and nematicity coexist in the phase diagram of many correlated systems, including iron-based superconductors. We investigate how Hund-driven correlations reshape boson-mediated superconductivity in a multiorbital nematic metal. We find that dynamical correlation effects beyond a quasiparticle-only description are essential to capture the robustness of superconductivity in the Hund regime. In the nematic phase, Hund correlations simultaneously enhance the orbital differentiation of the superconducting gaps and inhibit the most extreme nematic-driven orbital polarization and coherence collapse that would otherwise suppress pairing at strong coupling. A controlled cutoff analysis reveals a nontrivial, orbital-dependent buildup of the gaps, indicating that different frequency windows of the correlated spectrum contribute unevenly to pairing in the nematic Hund regime. This implies that pairing mechanisms with different characteristic boson energies can lead to distinct gap structures and trends.

items.title: Seismology of Glasses
items.summary: Aging and relaxation of glasses proceed through localized rearrangements that also generate long-ranged mechanical responses in their surroundings. We develop a theory that treats these rearrangements as internal microseismic sources, and thereby separates the direct effects emerging from an event from the effects from the far-field displacements it generates. These far-field disturbances propagate and relax through the viscoelastic medium through which they move, producing a stochastic background of weak but numerous perturbations at any given location. Combining the description of local events from the Random First Order Transition theory with this propagating background, we derive a unified equation for the dynamical structure factor of a relaxing glass. The theory identifies a finite wave-vector and time window in which the growing viscoelastic far-field disturbances can produce compressed exponential relaxation, which has been observed using X-ray photon correlation spectroscopy. At higher wave vectors that resolve local jumps, heterogeneity of the local event dynamics instead produces stretched exponential relaxation. The crossover between these behaviors depends on the event statistics and the scattering phase accumulated across the region reached through viscoelastic propagation from the numerous distant sources.

items.title: Complex pattern in periodically driven binary Quincke colloids
items.summary: Binary active systems offer a minimal platform for understanding how component heterogeneity organizes non-equilibrium structures. Here we show that in a binary Quincke system driven by a periodic square-wave electric field, a dynamic square lattice in which small particles occupy the lattice-cell centers which are surrounded by large particles emerges spontaneously. Particle-resolved trajectories reveal that the size separation arises from the mobility difference of large particles and small particles. Increasing the driving frequency reduces the single-cycle path lengths of both species and simultaneously decreases the lattice constant. These results show how size-dependent activity,density redistribution, and periodic forcing cooperate to generate tunable complex active patterns.

items.title: Static spin exchange-correlation kernel of the uniform electron gas at finite temperature
items.summary: We determine the temperature and momentum dependence of the static spin exchange--correlation kernel of the unpolarized three-dimensional uniform electron gas using variational diagrammatic Monte Carlo. The calculations cover metallic densities with Wigner--Seitz radii $r_s=1\!-\!4$ and temperatures $T/T_F=1/16\!-\!8$, where $T_F$ is the Fermi temperature. At low temperature, the calculated kernel approaches established ground-state parametrizations. Heating suppresses its Fermi-scale minimum and reduces its magnitude, while the relative momentum dependence evolves nonmonotonically through the warm-dense crossover. At the two highest temperatures studied, the spin kernel is nearly constant over $q \leq 2k_F$, where $k_F$ is the Fermi wave number. The charge kernel at $r_s=1$ retains pronounced momentum dependence under the same conditions, making a local approximation to the XC kernel more accurate in the spin channel over this interval. The directly sampled uniform response determines the XC free-energy curvature with respect to spin polarization, independently of a fitted polarization dependence. This curvature sets the interaction contribution to the free-energy cost of weak polarization and differs by several percent from the Groth--Dornheim--Bonitz parametrization at elevated temperatures. These results provide momentum-resolved reference data for finite-temperature spin-response theories and direct constraints on the spin dependence of thermal free-energy functionals.

items.title: Magnetic proximity beyond the interface: Layer-sequence-dependent exchange in WSe$_2$/CrI$_3$ heterostructures
items.summary: Magnetic proximity effects in transition metal dichalcogenide (TMD)/2D-magnet heterostructures are often described in terms of the magnetization of the interfacial magnetic layer. Here, we show that this picture is sufficient to describe the neutral-exciton valley splitting of the TMD, but incomplete for its hole-doped electronic structure. We study a gate-tunable van der Waals heterostructure composed of monolayer WSe$_2$ in direct contact with trilayer CrI$_3$. By combining spatially and helicity-resolved reflection-contrast spectroscopy with magnetic circular dichroism, we identify two distinct magnetic domains in the trilayer CrI$_3$: one with purely antiferromagnetic interlayer coupling and one with a mixed antiferromagnetic (AFM)/ferromagnetic~(FM) coupling. In both domains, the sign of the neutral-exciton valley splitting of WSe$_2$ switches with the magnetization reversal of the adjacent CrI$_3$ layer. In contrast, helicity-resolved positive-trion spectroscopy of WSe$_2$ reveals a qualitatively different response. While the AFM domain shows a strongly helicity-selective trion resonance, the mixed AFM/FM domain exhibits trion resonances in both helicities. This behavior disappears when all CrI$_3$ layers are aligned in a parallel magnetization direction. Our results demonstrate that charged excitons are sensitive to the full layer-resolved magnetic sequence of the adjacent 2D-magnet, revealing magnetic proximity beyond the interface.

items.title: In-Plane Differentiation and Out-of-Plane Coherence in Superconducting K$_{2-x}$Fe$_{4+y}$Se$_5$
items.summary: The structural link between superconductivity and anomalous $d_2$ diffraction signatures in K$_{2-x}$Fe$_{4+y}$Se$_5$ remains unresolved. Their appearance is accompanied by pronounced host-lattice evolution rather than a static structural background. Using high-resolution synchrotron X-ray diffraction, we show that excess Fe alters the vacancy-ordered host lattice, with structural differences between superconducting and nonsuperconducting states emerging before the $d_2$ features appear. All observed $d_2$ reflections can be described using two characteristic in-plane spacings and a nearly common low-temperature $c$ parameter. Temperature-dependent measurements reveal that superconductivity is associated with persistent in-plane differentiation and enhanced Fe-layer coherence along the $c$ axis. These results establish host-lattice evolution as the common structural origin linking the $d_2$ family and superconductivity, and suggest that the host-lattice differentiation identified here represents a structural analogue of the symmetry redistribution in FeSe.

items.title: Two-Way Coupled Dynamics of Quantized Vortex Bundle Formation in Spatially Periodic Normal-Fluid Turbulence
items.summary: Using fully coupled two-way simulations combining the vortex filament model with the Navier--Stokes equations, we discover that quantized vortices in superfluid $^4$He are systematically rolled up into coherent bundles within normal-fluid vortex tubes. Although co-rotating quantized vortices do not aggregate spontaneously, mutual friction with the normal fluid actively drives their bundling, directly inheriting the spatial hierarchy of classical turbulence. Mutual friction excites high-wavenumber normal-fluid vortex tubes adjacent to quantized vortices, while the superfluid forms a nested structure of thick low-wavenumber outer tubes and fine high-wavenumber inner tubes around the vortex lines. A distinct time lag between superfluid kinetic energy and dissipation fuels the energy cascade, giving rise to Kolmogorov's $k^{-5/3}$ spectrum. Crucially, bundle lifetimes are governed by the ratio of the local coupling time scale $t_\mathrm{cl}$ to the Kolmogorov dissipation time scale $τ_η$ ($t_\mathrm{cl}/τ_η< 20$), leading to enhanced thermal stability at higher temperatures. These findings establish a unified mechanism for two-fluid multiscale vortex organization.

items.title: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relation For a Multi-Phase Alternating Renewal Random Walk
items.summary: Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relations (TURs) impose universal bounds linking current precision to entropy production in nonequilibrium systems. While general bounds like the Proesmans--Van den Broeck (PV) relation provide a broad framework, they often remain loose for processes characterized by renewal events. In this work, we derive a generalized entropic bound for current fluctuations in renewal-reward processes. By utilizing a rigorous variance decomposition within the framework of renewal-reward theory, we obtain a model-independent bound that is not only rigorous but tighter than the standard PV relation. Notably, in the linear-response regime, our bound correctly scales with the renewal rate and identifies a precision penalty arising from cycle-length fluctuations. These results provide a physically informative constraint on the precision of run-and-tumble-type dynamics and highlight the universal limits of transport in complex stochastic walkers.

items.title: Magneto-optical signatures of plateau states in the kagome spin-ice HoAgGe
items.summary: Coupling of itinerant electrons to non-collinear spin structures in frustrated rare-earth magnets leads to unusual transport properties. While these complex magnetic orders are expected to modify the electronic structure, underlying microscopic mechanisms have been rarely identified. Using magnetoreflectance spectroscopy and \textit{ab initio} calculations, we reveal reconstructions of the electronic structure across the magnetization plateaus of the kagome spin-ice HoAgGe. We find an unusual optical anisotropy: a larger conductivity perpendicular to the kagome planes originating from the hybridization of Ho $4f$ flat bands with conduction electrons. Moreover, these flat bands are also responsible for the pronounced magnetoreflectance observed at the metamagnetic transitions. Most importantly, the magnetoreflectance behaves completely differently for excitations near the Fermi level and higher-energy interband transitions. The former, expected to sensitively probe variations in band topology near the Fermi level, shows abrupt non-monotonous changes between the magnetic states, while the interband excitations mimic the field dependence of the magnetization. These observations imply that in HoAgGe, the unusual magnetotransport likely reflects variation of band topology between plateau states. More generally, our study shows that heavy-electron bands near the Fermi level offer an efficient way to control the band structure and thereby the transport and optical properties of non-collinear magnets.

items.title: Thermally stimulated depolarization in hafnium oxide: experiment and numerical simulation
items.summary: This paper presents an experimental and theoretical study of thermally stimulated depolarization (TSD) in hafnium oxide. Three different models for the probability of trap ionization are considered: the Frenkel effect and two variants of the multiphonon trap ionization mechanism, the multiphonon ionization mechanism of isolated traps at low trap concentrations and phonon-assisted tunneling between neighboring traps at high trap concentrations. The best agreement between the TSD experiment and theory is observed for the multiphonon ionization mechanism of isolated traps. Similar thermal energies of electron and hole traps in HfO2 are obtained ~ 1.3 eV.

items.title: Pressure engineering of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape and exciton-charge interplay in semiconductor moiré superlattices
items.summary: Semiconductor moiré superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moiré potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. Here we integrate a diamond anvil pressure cell with high quality dual gated WSe2/WS2 twisted bilayers and perform cryogenic optical spectroscopy. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moiré intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. Moreover, we demonstrate efficient pressure control over the interplay between charges and both intralayer and interlayer excitons: the intralayer charge-transfer exciton becomes less sensitive to doping, likely due to reduced charge-transfer character; in contrast, the interlayer exciton exhibits enhanced exciton-charge repulsion. Our results establish hydrostatic pressure as a powerful tuning knob for engineering bosonic quasiparticles and Bose-Fermi interactions in moiré materials.

items.title: Classical Cellular Automaton for Measurement-Only Entanglement Transitions
items.summary: We introduce a generalized classical long-range stochastic cellular automaton that exactly captures the entanglement dynamics and transitions of a measurement-only monitored quantum system. The corresponding quantum model consists of a one-dimensional qubit chain subject to competing single-site and long-range Bell measurements, with separations drawn from a power-law distribution. At every step of each trajectory, the state remains a tensor product of Bell pairs and unpaired qubits, with bipartite entanglement entropy fully encoded in a classical matching of the sites. This exact representation allows us to solve the dynamics analytically in several limits and to determine the steady-state scaling of the entanglement entropy. We find volume-law, fractal, and area-law regimes. Numerical results show that these regimes persist beyond the analytically solvable limit. Because Bell measurement outcomes change only the Bell-state labels and leave the matching unchanged, all subsystem entropies are outcome independent, avoiding the exponential cost of trajectory postselection often encountered in experimental studies of measurement-induced entanglement dynamics.

items.title: How Long Is the Coast of a Neuron? Resolution-Dependent Interaction Order and Computational Capacity
items.summary: Mandlebrot's coastline paradox reframes measurement as a joint property of an object and its ruler. Here we ask how observational resolution shapes the apparent structure of neural computation. We introduce a scale-indexed decomposition that separates the predictive information captured by direct dependencies from the residual outside that model family. Exact constructions show that projection can convert higher-order dependence into pairwise structure. Projection can increase the direct fraction of surviving information even as total predictive information decreases. A schematic branch-to-soma cascade grounds these effects in local coincidence detection, saturating integration and somatic mixing. Resolving organized nonlinear subunits improves approximation and raises effective representational rank. In a nested hierarchy, these gains occur without increasing information about the target. This distinction separates information availability from access by a restricted readout. A point-neuron or direct population model therefore establishes an effective description at a specified scale. It does not uniquely identify the finer computation that generated the observed relation. Which resolution is adequate depends on the observable and perturbation of interest.

items.title: Why shaking faster does not untangle: frequency-selective extraction of filaments from tangled matter
items.summary: Tangles of soft filaments are ubiquitous, from living worm blobs to the cables in a desk drawer. How do such tangles, held together by friction and entanglement, respond when one embedded filament is shaken? We suspend disordered tangles of tunable cohesion and ordered stitched meshes from a single thread (the tether) and oscillate it vertically at fixed amplitude. Extraction peaks at an intermediate drive frequency ($\sim 15$ Hz) and declines at higher frequencies, although the peak drive acceleration grows quadratically. Here we combine experiments, high-speed imaging, and a tension-only spring-mass model to show that this non-monotonic response is set by timing rather than resonance. The extraction window is bounded below by a slackening threshold, where the peak drive acceleration exceeds gravity and the tether, slack for part of each cycle, creates a tensile impulse each time it snaps taut. The window is bounded above by a transmission crossover, where the transmission time across the tangle exceeds a quarter of the drive cycle, so that the tangle no longer responds as a whole and the drive's work dissipates internally. The slackening threshold depends only on the drive and gravity, while the transmission crossover is set only by the tangle's size and transmission speed. By tracing extraction to the overlap of impulse creation and impulse transmission, we identify a generic principle of driven filamentous matter and suggest frequency-selective routes to its disassembly.

items.title: Non-Hermitian Skin Effect from Radiative Coupling in a Reciprocal Chiral Medium
items.summary: We show that long-range radiative coupling in a passive chiral medium produces an unusual non-Hermitian skin effect in a chain of dipoles. The skin-mode profile consists of a long-range light-line branch-cut contribution, a non-exponential factor $1/[n(\ln n)^2]$ with $n$ being the site number. Finite-chain calculations show that part of the open-boundary spectrum contracts toward the Bloch spectrum, whereas the number of boundary-localized modes remains extensive. The retarded radiative coupling makes both the real-space profile and the finite-size spectral signatures of boundary localization depart from standard finite-range and pure exponential coupling theory.

items.title: Multiple Superconducting Phases under Pressure for Different Field Directions in UTe2
items.summary: The existence of multiple superconducting phases is a striking feature of UTe2, arising from the spin and orbital degrees of freedom and supporting a spin-triplet superconducting state. We present field-temperature phase diagrams under pressure for fields applied along the three principal crystallographic axes, as determined by AC calorimetry measurements. The pressure evolution of the multiple superconducting phases is highly anisotropic with respect to magnetic field direction, revealing rich superconducting phenomena arising from complex fluctuations.

items.title: ActMOF: Mapping Reticular Synthesis through Active Learning
items.summary: Reticular chemistry allows metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) to be designed from their building units, yet their synthesis remains constrained by sparse experimental data, noisy crystallization outcomes, and the absence of benchmarks for comparing active-learning strategies. While data-driven approaches such as Bayesian optimization (BO) can improve synthesis success rates, selecting appropriate optimizers beforehand for mapping MOF crystallization landscapes remains largely empirical. Here we present ActMOF, an experiment-grounded benchmark for comparing search strategies in aluminum-carboxylate MOF synthesis. ActMOF is emulated from experimentally measured microwave syntheses with each encoded condition assigned a crystallinity index calculated based on diffraction peak intensity and full width at half-maximum. By benchmarking policies guided by Gaussian processes (GP), tree ensembles and large language models (LLM), ActMOF placed the GP family among the leading policies for active learning in sparse synthesis landscapes. It then demonstrated transferability by guiding the microwave synthesis of six reticularly related aluminum MOFs. All six campaigns gave crystalline products within a fixed budget of 12 experiments each, and established a reusable testbed for AI-driven MOF synthesis.

items.title: Ultrasmall (3,0) carbon nanotube: a superconducting unit with strong electron-phonon coupling
items.summary: Based on density-functional first-principles calculations, we study the electronic structures, lattice dynamics, and electron-phonon coupling (EPC) properties of the ultrasmall one-dimensional (3,0) carbon nanotube (CNT). Our studies reveal that the (3,0) CNT hosts characteristic collective phonon modes, in which the corresponding atomic vibrations can significantly modulate the electronic self-consistent potential and induce strong EPC. Our results further show that the (3,0) CNT exhibits robust phonon-mediated superconductivity under ambient pressure, with a superconducting transition temperature reaching $\sim$ 33 K ($μ^*$ = 0.10). We also find that although hole doping enhances the density of states (DOS) near the Fermi level, it simultaneously hardens the strongly coupled phonon modes and suppresses the total EPC. This result indicates that phonons play a more crucial role in the superconductivity of ultrasmall CNTs rather than the DOS alone. Therefore, we suggest that the ultrasmall (3,0) CNT can serve as a superconducting unit hosting phonon modes with strong EPC, and propose a strategy for discovering new phonon-mediated superconductors by identifying superconducting units.

items.title: Phase Stability and Anisotropic Superconductivity in Ternary M2B4C2 (M=Ca, Mg) Monolayer
items.summary: In this work, we investigate the phase stability, electronic structure, and superconducting properties of the two-dimensional ternary borocarbides MB$_4$C$_2$ (M = Ca, Mg) using first-principles calculations and fully anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg theory. Ab initio molecular dynamics, phonon dispersion, and elastic constant calculations confirm that both monolayers are dynamically, thermally, and mechanically stable. Electronic structure analysis reveals an intrinsic metallic nature with a multiband Fermi surface, where states near the $Γ$ point are dominated by in-plane B-$p_x$, $p_y$ orbitals, while zone-boundary states are primarily derived from out-of-plane B-$p_z$ orbitals. The electron-phonon coupling is determined to be $λ= 0.64$ for both materials, driven by the rigid covalent B-B and B-C honeycomb networks. By solving the anisotropic Eliashberg equations, we predict that CaB$_4$C$_2$ and MgB$_4$C$_2$ are nodeless two-gap superconductors with critical temperatures ($T_c$) of 33.4 K and 33.8 K, respectively, at a Coulomb pseudopotential of $μ= 0.10$. Furthermore, the superconducting state remains robust under increased Coulomb repulsion ($μ= 0.13$), retaining elevated $T_c$ values of 31.2 K and 30.9 K, respectively. These findings establish MB$_4$C$_2$ monolayers as promising candidates for nanoscale superconducting applications and enrich the family of two-dimensional multigap superconductors.

items.title: Dynamic Magnetic Pair-Density Function of a One-Dimensional Ferromagnet
items.summary: The dynamic magnetic pair-density function (DymPDF) $D_{\rm M}(r, E)$ is derived by extending the static magnetic pair distribution function (mPDF) to finite energy transfer. The analytical DymPDF of a one-dimensional Heisenberg ferromagnet is obtained from the magnon dispersion and compared with simulations performed using {\textsc SpinW}. Excellent agreement is achieved for energy dependence of the nearest-neighbor spin-pair correlation, demonstrating that the DymPDF changes sign at the magnon-mode transition occurring at one-half of the maximum magnon energy. The r-dependence of DymPDF at low energy is also reproduced with a model including magnon correlation length and Fourier-termination effects. These results establish the theoretical foundation of DymPDF analysis for investigating local spin dynamics in magnetic materials.

items.title: Odd-to-Even-Layer Switch of Spontaneous Excitonic State in $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ Thin Films
items.summary: $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ is a candidate of high temperature excitonic condensates with spontaneous exciton formation in addition to its charge density wave (CDW). However, direct observation and manipulation of this electron-hole paring state formation is still lacking. Here, using varying-temperature angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (VT-ARPES), we observe a distinct odd-to-even-layer switch of spontaneous exciton state formation with the evident correlated band structure in $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ thin films. While the odd-layer $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ films show a sharp band structure in single-particle picture superimposed by CDW renormalization, in the even-layer $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ films, the full-filling valence band (VB) opens a distinct notch at the top, and the conductive band (CB) shows a significant extra signal extending above Fermi level with spectra broadening. These features indicate that the extra holes (notched VB) and electrons (broadening CB above Fermi level) form spontaneous excitons in even-layer $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$. Based on a correlated electron-hole model extracted from the tight-binding description, we reproduce the characterized band structures with spontaneous exciton formation, where the interlayer inter-band coupling in $\rm{TiSe_{2}}$ plays a key role, which leads to an odd-to-even-layer switch of the excitonic state formation. Our results provide direct evidences of the spontaneous exciton formation, promising an excitonic condensate as versatile platform for realizing Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and investigating novel correlated phenomena.

items.title: Dynamics of spinor Bose-Einstein condensates close to spin-spatial resonances
items.summary: We develop a coupled-channel framework to describe the dynamics of spinor Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs), with particular emphasis on the behavior near resonances between spin dynamics and spatial excitations. Taking advantage of the disparity between the spin-dependent and spin-independent scattering lengths in typical spinor BECs, the Bogoliubov modes of the spin-independent part of the full system Hamiltonian provide an efficient set of basis functions for describing the system dynamics in a coupled-channel framework. For quadratic Zeeman shifts far from any resonance, the system can be described by a single spatial wavefunction during the spin dynamics, i.e., the so-called single-mode approximation holds. By tuning the quadratic Zeeman shift, we find resonant excitations of the Bogoliubov modes, which can be classified into two categories: those with particle-hole correlations and those without particle-hole correlations. We show that the beyond-quadratic-order terms that are neglected in standard Bogoliubov theories become increasingly important for capturing the long-time dynamics of the system near resonances. The coupled-channel framework is benchmarked against results from 1D Gross-Pitaevskii equation simulations. The framework developed in this work not only provides a numerically efficient tool for describing spinor BEC dynamics governed by different length scales, but also provides a clean physical interpretation of resonance phenomena in spinor BECs. Applications of this approach to other systems and extensions to the beyond-mean-field regime are also discussed.

items.title: How deterministic trajectories and their fluctuations underlie allele-frequency statistics in the strong-selection regime
items.summary: We determine statistics of allele-frequency trajectories across replicate populations. Defining $R = 2N_e|s|$ where $N_e$ is the effective population size and $s$ is the additive selection coefficient of a focal allele, we focus on strong selection which corresponds to $R \gg 1$. Strong selection does not require large selection coefficients: in populations of realistic size, it can readily arise from small selection coefficients. Our analysis concerns a biallelic locus over timescales on which mutation can be neglected. Every allele-frequency trajectory belongs to one of two absorbing classes: fixation or loss. When $R$ is large, individual allele-frequency trajectories can appear nearly deterministic. This does not imply that an approximation of allele-frequency statistics can be based on a single deterministic trajectory. For a beneficial allele, the deterministic trajectory approaches fixation, yet a non-negligible fraction of stochastic trajectories may be lost. Ignoring trajectories that achieve loss can produce severely erroneous statistics. We address this by conditioning separately on the eventual loss and eventual fixation of the focal allele. This yields an outcome-conditioned representation of a statistic. In the strong-selection regime, we apply a small-noise expansion that reasonably captures transient behaviours of statistics while recovering their exact long-time limits. We illustrate results with numerical examples for the mean allele frequency and its variance. The biological interpretation of this work is that, even under strong selection, both trajectory types are of importance. We provide a simple framework for calculating time-dependent allele-frequency statistics relevant to experimental evolution, longitudinal population-genomic data, and the dynamics of alleles driving selective sweeps.

items.title: Evidence for hidden order and its potential correlation with electron-hole asymmetry in iridate superlattices
items.summary: Hidden order refers to an order that shapes the properties of quantum materials yet remains difficult to identify. Here we report signatures of a hidden order in doped iridate superlattices through an unexpected electron-hole asymmetry in the coupling between the insulating state and the antiferromagnetic (AFM) state. While carrier doping suppresses both states, they remain coupled in the electron-doped regime but decouple in the hole-doped regime. Structural analysis rules out octahedral rotation and tilting as the dominant origin of this asymmetry. Instead, magnetic characterization reveals evidences of a hidden order that only appears in the hole-doped regime. This hidden order emerges above TN and is closely associated with the AFM state, coinciding with an exceptionally strong magnetic scattering intensity and an anomalously robust magnetic coherence. Our results highlight that hole-doped iridates can be a promising platform for exploring hidden and unconventional ordering phenomena in spin-orbit-entangled quantum materials.

items.title: Photonic half-semimetals with dual semimetal-insulator topology
items.summary: Abstract Topological wave systems have largely evolved along two distinct paradigms: gapless topological semimetals and gapped topological insulators. While topological semimetals support bulk transport, they generally lack intrinsic selectivity among propagation channels; topological insulators enable robust transport but confine it to narrow interfaces, limiting spatial utilization. Here, we theoretically demonstrate and experimentally realize time-reversal-invariant spin-valley photonic half-semimetals (HSMs), which exhibit a dual semimetal-insulator topology within a single bulk band structure. In HSMs, the bandgap closes selectively in spin-valley space: for a given spin (valley), one valley (spin) is semimetallic while the other remains insulating. This coexistence of spin- and valley-resolved gapless and gapped band structures makes HSMs fundamentally distinct from both conventional semimetals and insulators. As a defining bulk phenomenon, an HSM functions as a spin-valley-locked beam splitter, intrinsically enabling valley-selective spin routing. Moreover, when four complementary HSMs are assembled into a periodic superlattice, the same dual topology enables reciprocal spin-valley-resolved multilane helical transport with 100% spatial utilization. These results establish HSMs as a platform for selective bulk wave control and multichannel topological transport beyond conventional topological phases.

items.title: Unified structural origin of functionality in spiral skyrmions revealed by 3D electron tomography
items.summary: Abstract Ferroelectric skyrmions exhibit a range of emergent phenomena, including collective dynamics, negative capacitance, and a strong electric-field-induced second-harmonic generation response. However, three-dimensional (3D) atomic-scale configurations of skyrmions are unclarified yet, making the relationship between the physical functionalities and their underlying structural origin remains elusive. Here, using atomic-scale electron tomography, we experimentally resolve the 3D structure of polar skyrmion for the first time in PbTiO 3 /SrTiO 3 superlattice. On the basis of large-data image acquisition with more than 95,000 3D coordinates of atoms, we visualize that the core of the skyrmions exhibit an upward spiraling morphology. By quantitatively analyzing the ferroelectric polarization and lattice distortion, we uncover an unconventional decoupling between the two at the skyrmion wall, where the polarization is suppressed, accompanied by a local enhancement of tetragonality exceeding 5% at the center of the wall. This increased tetragonality modifies the local free-energy landscape, enhancing the negative-capacitance response and field sensitivity at the skyrmion wall. The polar skyrmion wall hosts a concentration of emergent physical properties, thereby providing a unified structural origin for the functionalities and physical behaviors of skyrmions. This work establishes a real space basis for understanding the physical properties of polar skyrmions.

items.title: How does the brain do more with less energy?
Evidence of large-scale and room-temperature stair-stepped quantum spin Hall states in Bi4Br4
items.summary: Abstract Topological insulators host exotic quantum phenomena such as the quantum spin Hall (QSH) effect, which enables dissipationless one-dimensional edge conduction. Realizing such states at room temperature and on a macroscopic scale is essential for energy-efficient electronics and quantum technologies, yet remains a fundamental challenge due to material limitations. Here, using microwave impedance microscopy, we directly visualize robust conductive channels persisting up to 300 K in α -Bi 4 Br 4 nanowires. Their stability and scalability are likely enabled by a “stair-stepped” stacking configuration on the side facets, a multilayer geometry in which QSH edge states from individual layers remain spatially decoupled. This configuration circumvents the stringent alignment and layer-number constraints of previous proposals, allowing robust stair-stepped QSH (SS-QSH) conduction in structures several micrometers long and hundreds of nanometers high. Magnetic-field- and temperature-dependent measurements are consistent with the topological nature of these conductive channels, as further supported by our theoretical analysis. Crucially, the conductance peaks and bulk signals scale with nanowire height, verifying the stair-stepped origin. Our results are also successfully reproduced by finite-element analysis simulations. This work establishes α -Bi 4 Br 4 as a practical platform for high-temperature topological electronics and demonstrates a generalizable stacking strategy for designing scalable QSH systems.

items.title: Robust quasi-bound states in the continuum in bilayer terahertz metasurface with S4 point-group symmetry
items.summary: Abstract Metasurface-based bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable exceptional spatiotemporal control of light and substantially enhance light–matter interactions, making them highly attractive for applications in sensing, nonlinear optics, and integrated photonics. However, conventional BICs in single-layer metasurfaces rely on in-plane symmetry and are highly susceptible to structural perturbations, offering limited design flexibility and constraining both their robustness and functional diversity. To overcome these limitations, we theoretically propose and experimentally demonstrate a new class of symmetry-protected quasi-BICs in bilayer terahertz metasurfaces. These states are realized by coupling in-plane rotational and out-of-plane reflective symmetries through S 4 point-group operations. Moreover, we show that such QBICs exhibit strong robustness against structural defects and fabrication imperfections. This work overcomes the robustness limitations of conventional single-layer metasurface BICs and establishes a general design paradigm for photonic devices that harness BICs with enhanced stability and scalability.

items.title: Deciphering Critical Transition for AKI Deterioration by STIfuse: Fusing Dynamic and Static Representations
items.summary: Abstract Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a life-threatening condition with notably high in-hospital mortality, characterized by a three-phase progression: a relatively stable state (without imminent life threat), a critical pre-deterioration state (the time window which may be identified and in which timely intervention could prevent upcoming irreversible deterioration), and a deteriorated state (severe conditions such as death or rescue events). Accurate early prediction of AKI deterioration and deciphering the critical transition remain challenging because of complex, high-dimensional, noisy, and incomplete clinical data, as well as limited mechanistic understanding of disease progression. To solve this problem, we propose STIfuse (Spatiotemporal Information fusion), a unique dual-view framework that integrates deep learning (DL) and spatiotemporal information transformation (STI) based on Takens’ embedding theorem and critical slowing down (CSD) theory. The DL backbone encodes multi-dimensional static representations to capture structural dependencies, while the STI branch transforms high-dimensional spatial information into a low-dimensional dynamic representation. These views are fused by a multivariate Gaussian distribution: the means capture statistical levels for diagnosis, and the covariances reflect collective physiological fluctuations for early deterioration prediction. An optimal-transport-distance-based contrastive loss is employed to learn discriminative dynamic features between ˈcriticalˈ and ˈstableˈ states. Pretrained on the MIMIC-IV dataset and validated on five external cohorts (including MIMIC-III (with two independent cohorts), eICU, HiRID, and NWICU), STIfuse demonstrated superior performance in predicting 72-hour deterioration. Further analysis of single-cell multi-omics data study uncovered inflammatory cascades linking comorbidities to AKI. STIfuse provides an interpretable, robust and scalable framework for early warning of AKI deterioration prediction, highlighting its potential in utility and scalability for clinical foundation models.

items.title: Resonant interactions in the $α$-FPUT lattice with site-dependent coefficients
items.summary: The wave turbulence framework has proven to be an effective tool for analyzing certain features of nonlinear energy transfer in one-dimensional nonlinear chains. In this work, we extend this approach to the $α$-FPUT problem when the spring stiffness $χ$ and the nonlinear coefficient $α$ are site-dependent. Although three-wave interactions are non-resonant for constant coefficients, their spatial modulation gives rise to a non-trivial resonant manifold. In this framework, we derive a new kinetic equation that suggests the possibility of substantially faster thermalization with respect to the constant coefficient case. The new kinetic equation includes also an extra term that can be associated to the Bragg-scattering mechanism, which promotes the isotropization of the wave-action spectral density function. We corroborate these results with direct numerical simulations, confirming the radically faster thermalization pathway in the presence of random coefficients.

items.title: Mutual Information of Measurement in Conformal Field Theories
items.summary: The mutual information of measurement of a local operator between two spatial regions characterizes the reduction in the uncertainty of measurement outcomes in one region given the outcome in the other. We study the Rényi-Shannon mutual information of measurement in conformal field theories (CFTs). Explicit calculations for scalar primaries and descendants in large $N$ CFTs are performed in the two extreme limits of the intervals being adjacent or largely separated. The results depend on only the cross ratio and the scaling dimension $Δ$ of the operator being measured, with striking similarities to the mutual information of entanglement. We find a surprising quadratic dependence as $(Δ-1/2)^2$ for adjacent intervals. This dependence superficially seems to violate the information processing inequality, which we discuss and resolve. We also offer a holographic interpretation of the mutual information of measurement.

items.title: Chern insulator optics
items.summary: Chern insulators have optical properties that are strikingly different than ordinary chiral media. Unlike the natural optical activity of the latter, which is a finite-wavelength effect arising from spatial dispersion, the optical activity of a Chern insulator is already present in the long-wavelength limit, and exhibits a striking directional asymmetry in the propagation of circularly polarized light. We study this unnatural optical activity using a recently developed field theory for Chern insulators. For bulk Chern insulators, we derive the normal-incidence transmission and reflection coefficients of multilayer structures, identify the associated Faraday and Kerr angles, and show that these optical rotations provide a direct optical signature of topology at low frequencies. We also show that an interface between bulk Chern insulators can act as a kind of mirror, completely reflecting light at normal incidence when the Chern invariants have opposite signs. Moving to a more realistic model of a two-dimensional current sheet, we study the Faraday and Kerr effects in a thin film of $\mathrm{Mn}\mathrm{Bi}_2\mathrm{Te}_4$ in its Chern insulator phase. The predicted rotations are many orders of magnitude larger than those of optically active media of comparable thickness that are topologically trivial.

items.title: Signatures of symmetry-stabilized Dirac fermions in correlated oxide CaNbO3 thin films
items.summary: Symmetry-protected electronic states in correlated oxides offer a route to combining topology, lattice tunability, and many-body interactions, but creating such topological electronic states in complex oxides remains challenging. Here, we show that oxygen octahedral rotations provide a symmetry-control parameter for stabilizing Dirac-related electronic states in epitaxial CaNbO3 films. By comparing compressively strained tetragonal films and relaxed orthorhombic films, we demonstrate that distinct octahedral rotation patterns preserve nonsymmorphic symmetry and lead to distinct transport signatures consistent with Dirac-like electronic states. The films exhibit metallic transport with high mobility of 138,000 cm2 V-1 s-1, multichannel conduction, and Shubnikov-de Haas oscillations from small high-mobility Fermi pockets. Landau-fan diagram analysis indicates finite Berry-phase contributions, while first-principles calculations reveal a strain-driven evolution from nodal-line band crossings in the orthorhombic phase to Dirac-electron band features in the tetragonal phase. These results establish oxygen octahedral symmetry as a design knob for engineering topological electronic states in correlated perovskite oxides.

items.title: Atomic ironing for conformal interfaces in freestanding oxide nanomembranes
items.summary: Atomically well-defined interfaces are essential for realizing functional interlayer coupling in stacked and twisted oxide heterostructures, yet transferred freestanding oxides can develop structural inhomogeneities, including local curvatures, interfacial voids, and incomplete contacts with substrates. Here, we demonstrate that these transfer-induced structural disorders and imperfections evolve substantially and can be suppressed by post-transfer thermal treatments, yielding bulk-like crystalline freestanding oxide nanomembranes. Using freestanding SrTiO3 membranes as a model system, we report a systematic understanding of the role of "atomic ironing" and the associated evolution of lattice mosaicity, interfacial roughness, and optical bandgap. We further demonstrate atomically bonded conformal interfaces in twisted SrTiO3 heterostructures, highlighting the importance of post-transfer thermal processes. These results establish a synthetic strategy to restore the structural integrity and intrinsic bulk-like functionality of freestanding oxide nanomembranes, enabling stacked, twisted, and heterogeneously integrated oxide architectures with atomically well-defined interfaces for emerging quantum functionalities.

items.title: Spectral signatures of spin textures and the emergence of a pseudogap
items.summary: Periodic solids with strongly interacting electrons display phenomena -- from Mott localization to high-temperature superconductivity -- that escape conventional band theory. Efforts to address this unconventional physics have been typically cast in the language of Green's function theories and the associated frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies capturing strong correlations beyond the reach of mean-field theories. Here, we underscore that frequency- and momentum-dependent self-energies emerge also from mean-field solutions that break translational symmetry, and that these self-energies can display the characteristic fingerprints of strong correlations for certain, physically meaningful, spatial patterns. We showcase this perspective by studying the paradigmatic case of the 2D Hubbard model. We find that already at the mean-field level the doped antiferromagnet displays, in addition to stripes, many quasi-degenerate self-consistent solutions with antiferromagnetic textures organized into antiphase domains separated by hole-rich interfaces, reminiscent of the phase-separation scenario. Remarkably, these solutions map into spectral functions that display very distinctively the phenomenology of the pseudogap, including the nodal-antinodal dichotomy of the self-energy, Fermi arcs, and a complementary Luttinger surface. The result is a conceptually simple description of such an intricate many-body state: the pseudogap emerges as the momentum-space spectral portrait of the real-space interplay between antiferromagnetic domains and the metallic interfaces, which echoes the role of spin-fluctuations identified by nonperturbative methods.

items.title: Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
items.summary: Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped, among other results, to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two ensembles allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and free-probability methods, the generic case of independently random Hamiltonian and dissipative components requires a novel framework that combines operator-valued free probability with sequential noise averaging. For this ensemble, our approach preserves the underlying tensor-product structure of the Lindblad operator and derives a general equation for the spectral boundary. We characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing and explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component.

items.title: Enhanced Critical Currents and Irreversibility Fields in YBa$_2$Cu$_4$O$_8$ Films through Ca-Substitution
items.summary: The intrinsic carrier concentration of superconducting materials may not be optimal, and different superconducting properties may have distinct optimal doping levels. Here, we show that Ca substitution increases the hole concentration in intrinsically underdoped epitaxial (Y$_{1-x}$Ca$_x$)Ba$_2$Cu$_4$O$_8$ (YCa124) films with $x \leq 0.10$, driving YCa124 toward optimal doping, increasing $T_c$ and $J_c$. At 40 K, 10% Ca doping increases $J_c$ by factors of 2.4 and 10 at 0.03 and 6 T, respectively, compared with the undoped film. The field dependence of $J_c$ follows $J_c \propto B^{-0.5}$, independent of Ca content, indicating that Ca substitution does not alter the dominant pinning mechanism. This field dependence is consistent with pinning by planar Y-125 stacking-fault intergrowths observed by electron microscopy. In addition, Ca substitution slows thermally activated vortex motion (creep) at $T \gtrsim 15$ K, while at lower temperatures the creep rate $S$ shows an unusual decrease with increasing field. Finally, we consider how doping tunes the upper bound on $J_c$, set by the depairing current density $J_d$, and the lower bound on creep, set by the Ginzburg parameter $G_i$. We find positive correlations between $J_c$ and $J_d$, and between $S$ and $G_i$, and compare them with trends across a broad range of superconductors.

items.title: On the Mathematical Structure of Helical Shear in Anelastic Continua
items.summary: We study helical shear of a thick-walled tube made of an incompressible, isotropic hyper-anelastic solid carrying a radially symmetric distribution of axial screw dislocations. Through the Bilby--Kröner--Lee decomposition, the dislocations are encoded in a Weitzenböck material manifold, whose Riemannian metric alone enters the elastic response. Equilibrium reduces at each radius to an algebraic system for the azimuthal and axial shear strains, whose cross terms are proportional to the dislocation strength and to the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant; the two shear modes therefore couple only in the presence of dislocations. Exact solutions are obtained for neo-Hookean, Fung--Demiray, Gent, Knowles, and Mooney--Rivlin materials, and numerical ones for Gent--Gent materials. The universal relations of Horgan and Saccomandi are extended to dislocated generalized neo-Hookean tubes. Dislocations stiffen the tube when the strain energy stiffens with the first invariant, couple the two shear modes chirally when it depends on the second, and may restrict admissibility: they cap the dislocation strength in Gent and Gent--Gent materials, and contract the admissible traction region in Knowles materials with power-law index below n = 1/2. A weakly nonlinear analysis to third order in the applied tractions and dislocation strength shows that, at first order (linear elasticity), the dislocations leave the shear response unaffected while carrying a residual stress. The chiral coupling enters at second order, through the dependence of the strain energy on the second invariant, so that every dislocated material couples the modes as the Mooney--Rivlin solid with the same second- and third-order moduli. At third order, no new coupling arises; the modes interact through stiffness corrections involving the fourth-order modulus, which the dislocations further correct mode by mode.

items.title: Selective Control and Imaging of Higgs and Goldstone Modes with a Quantum Simulator
items.summary: We realize the mesoscopic Bose-Hubbard model at unit-filling on a two-dimensional array of transmon qubits and selectively excite collective modes associated with amplitude or phase fluctuations of the superfluid order parameter. We identify these modes respectively as the Higgs and Goldstone modes using complementary local observables, extracted from measuring the number of particles on each site. Modulation of the coupling between sites excites the Higgs mode, which we detect via the density of doubly occupied sites. In contrast, modulation of the local chemical potential with an appropriately chosen spatial profile excites the lowest-frequency Goldstone mode, which we detect via changes in the local density. The two modes have different symmetries and do not couple to one another. By varying the system geometry, we characterize the impact of finite system size on the evolution of both modes. In the thermodynamic limit, decay into a continuum of lower-energy excitations can obscure the Higgs response. In our mesoscopic system, however, the finite system size leads to spectral gaps and allows us to detect the Higgs mode as a coherent, long-lived excitation. Our work demonstrates how finite quantum simulators can isolate and probe physical phenomena that become difficult to resolve in the thermodynamic, large-scale limit.

items.title: On optimal Wannier decay in dimension three
items.summary: For a Chern nontrivial Bloch bundle over the three torus, we construct an orthonormal Wannier basis with the optimal pointwise decay $\mathcal{O}(|x|^{-5/2})$. All but one of the generators decay exponentially. This resolves the question left open in arXiv:2505.01999.

items.title: Zigzag Graphene Nanoribbons as a Majorana Platform
items.summary: Graphene nanoribbons support a variety of electronic phases that can be tuned via external stimuli. In particular, zigzag graphene nanoribbons exhibit an antiferromagnetic insulating ground state which can transition to a half-metallic phase under a transverse electric field or when embedded in hexagonal boron nitride. Here, we develop a simple model of a heterostructure composed of a half-metallic zigzag graphene nanoribbon coupled with an Ising superconductor. We demonstrate that an Ising superconductor's s-wave spin-singlet pairing gap component can induce a spin-triplet, odd-parity pairing gap in the half-metallic phase of the nanoribbon via proximity coupling. The resulting superconducting phase is topologically nontrivial, with gate-tunable transitions that enable the emergence of Majorana zero modes.

items.title: Cavity-assisted dynamic nuclear polarisation
items.summary: Dynamic nuclear polarisation transfers polarisation from electron to nuclear spins by relying on a dissipative channel. Here we introduce a cavity-based DNP mechanism which uses the radiative relaxation of the electronic spin through the Purcell effect to bring about the nuclear spin polarisation. We implement this protocol on an ensemble of bismuth donor spins (I=9/2, S=1/2) in isotopically purified silicon coupled to a superconducting resonator. A single cycle, combining adiabatic microwave and radio-frequency pulses with Purcell relaxation, increases a target ground state's population by a factor of $1.79\pm0.04$; a cumulative enhancement of $4.6\pm0.2$ is reached with additional cycles, to be compared with the theoretical limit of ninefold set by the degeneracy of the ground manifold. We explain this difference by the competition between Purcell and intrinsic relaxation on the one hand and a collective effect that slows down the electronic spin radiative decay as the nuclear spin population grows on the other hand. Our results place radiative DNP as an available mechanism at millikelvin temperatures where phonon-mediated relaxation is frozen.

items.title: Symmetry-selected extreme shear compliance in a stable carbon monolayer
items.summary: Solids that are stiff to most loads and extremely compliant to one are normally built, not found. That internal atomic relaxation lowers elastic constants is textbook; what has remained untested is whether it can be driven far enough to separate the elastic scales of a crystal by an order of magnitude while leaving it mechanically stable. Density functional theory calculations of the complete in-plane elastic tensor of four non-hexagonal carbon monolayers sharing a square lattice metric show that it can: their longitudinal stiffnesses agree to within a factor of two while their shear constants span more than a factor of fifty. Twin T-graphene, previously reported as elastically isotropic from normal strains alone, is the extreme case, with $C_{66}=3.03$~N\,m$^{-1}$, nearly fifty times below graphene, at an axial stiffness typical of semiconducting monolayers, and a soft Kelvin eigenvalue a factor of $29$ below the others while the Born criteria hold. Symmetry confines the strain-induced relaxation to the $B_{2g}$ sector, a counter-torsion of the carbon sublayers about the short mid-plane bonds that removes $96\%$ of the clamped-ion shear stiffness with almost no bond stretching and leaves the semiconducting gap intact. Transverse acoustic phonons, finite-temperature dynamics, and large-deformation simulations show that the channel survives beyond the harmonic, zero-temperature limit. Because the selection rule is a point-group statement rather than a chemical one, it yields a screening criterion for other crystals and other strain components.

items.title: Pseudo-relativistic fermions and topological states in zinc-blende semiconductors and their heterostructures (Habilitation thesis)
items.summary: Tracing my scientific path from many-body physics in semiconductor nanostructures to topological quantum matter, this Habilitation à diriger des recherches (HDR) memoir presents only part of my research since defending two PhD theses in Toulouse and Nizhny Novgorod in 2011. Focusing on pseudo-relativistic fermions and topological states in zinc-blende semiconductors and their heterostructures, it highlights my independent research program: identifying physical problems, developing predictive theories, and initiating new directions with experimentalists. The first part addresses Kane fermions in bulk HgCdTe: temperature-driven band inversion, domain-wall states, the collapse of Landau levels in crossed electric and magnetic fields, and disorder-induced topological transitions. The second examines pressure-, temperature-, and disorder-driven phase transitions in single and double HgTe quantum wells (QWs), including bilayer-graphene-like semimetals and a two-dimensional higher-order topological insulator (2D HOTI) phase beyond the minimal BHZ model. The third develops three-layer InAs/Ga(In)Sb QWs as a III-V platform for massless Dirac fermions, large-gap quantum spin Hall insulators, 2D HOTI phases, and semimetals with quadratic band touching, and discusses InAs$_{x}$Sb$_{1-x}$/InAs$_{y}$Sb$_{1-y}$ heterostructures as a promising alternative. Several of these predictions are supported by experimental observations, including quantized helical edge transport up to 60 K and the unconventional quantum Hall effect. Defended on March 25, 2026, at the University of Montpellier. Jury: Michel GOIRAN (chair and rapporteur, LNCMI-CNRS, Toulouse); Alexey KAVOKIN (rapporteur, Westlake University, Hangzhou); Robson FERREIRA (rapporteur, LPENS-CNRS, Paris); Alexei BARANOV (member, IES-CNRS, Montpellier); Benoit JOUAULT and Frédéric TEPPE (members, L2C-CNRS, Montpellier).

items.title: The odometer in subcritical activated random walk
items.summary: We consider the activated random walk particle system, a model of self-organized criticality, on $\mathbb{Z}$ with i.i.d.-Bernoulli initial configuration. We show that at subcritical density, the system's odometer function, which counts the number of actions taken at each site, has a stretched exponential tail. It follows that the expected odometer at each site is finite.

items.title: Kinetic Equations and Turbulence in Large $N$ Vector and SYK-like Models
items.summary: We apply large $N$ expansion techniques to derive kinetic equations for strongly coupled, far-from-equilibrium field theories with $O(N)$ symmetry. For large $N$ vector models, the quasi-classical approximation holds. Incorporating arbitrary momentum-dependent interactions, we show the dynamics obey the standard kinetic equation, with the scattering amplitude given by the retarded propagator of the auxiliary Hubbard-Stratonovich field. This has broad applications to systems like spin wave and Langmuir ion-acoustic turbulence. For large $N$ random coupling (SYK-like) models in $d$ dimensions, leading-order melon diagrams induce order-one propagator renormalization and finite spectral width. The corresponding kinetic equation, unlike those for standard weakly interacting systems, does not have a local-in-time collision integral. We find evidence for a stationary, scale-invariant infrared solution, revealing a potentially novel strong turbulence scaling exponent.

items.title: High-fidelity k$\cdot$p representations of first-principles electronic band structures through covariant renormalization
items.summary: The k$\cdot$p method can be applied directly to first-principles energies and momentum matrix elements, but the resulting models converge slowly with the number of bands and are inexact wherever the underlying Hamiltonian is nonlocal. We show that both limitations can be largely removed by renormalizing the eigenvalue spectra of the Hermitian momentum matrices. These spectra are gauge invariant, and are identical along symmetry-related directions; hence scaling the recurring magnitudes provides a modest set of parameters that preserves degeneracies and crystal symmetry without needing to construct a symmetry-adapted basis. We choose to renormalize the models against reference eigenvalues and band velocities on rays out of a high-symmetry point. For GaP, a 15-band model can reproduce the band structure in the near-gap reference regions within a few meV. For zincblende and wurtzite AlN, similar accuracy requires 30- or 85-band models, which in the case of zincblende is traced to the strong warping in the [110] direction. The scheme readily generalizes to rocksalt PbTe, which includes spin-orbit coupling, and has $L$-centered valence- and conduction-band extrema. Further, we demonstrate, for GaP, how compact four-band Hamiltonians can be obtained by downfolding within the same renormalization scheme. Moreover, by changing the fitting regime to encompass the entire Brillouin zone, the scheme can be used to generate full-zone models that reproduce the density of states. A practical use of the method is illustrated with a 59-band k$\cdot$p model for GaP, which can be evaluated on meshes far denser than the reference calculation, that in turn can be used both to resolve fine features in the density of states and to compute the hole conductivity at low temperature.

items.title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
items.summary: Transparent conductors are key functional materials in modern optoelectronic devices. Their performance is governed by an inherent trade-off between optical transparency and electrical conductivity. Correlated metallic oxides offer an attractive workaround to this compromise, where narrow partially-filled bands provide high conductivity, while the absence of visible-range transitions enables optical transparency. Despite this promise, transparency and conductivity remain coupled through carrier density and electronic coherence. Here, we use proximity to a metal-insulator transition (MIT) as a design principle for engineering this balance in correlated-oxide transparent conductors. Epitaxial Ti-substituted $SrVO_3$ films serve as a model platform where the optical window and metallicity are tuned simultaneously. We demonstrate and explain a systematic broadening of the optical window to regimes relevant for silicon photovoltaics. This gain is counterbalanced by carrier depletion and disorder, which drive the loss of coherent transport near the composition-driven MIT. A Haacke figure-of-merit analysis identifies the optimal composition range near the MIT, where the loss of metallic transport is accompanied by persistent near-Fermi-level spectral weight, indicating disorder-assisted localization together with correlation-driven spectral-weight redistribution. These findings establish proximity to an MIT as a general materials-design strategy, using electronic filling as a tuning knob for the transparency-conductivity balance in correlated-oxide transparent conductors.

items.title: Work statistics of sudden quantum quenches: A random matrix theory perspective on Gaussianity and its deviations
items.summary: We show that, for sudden quenches, the work distribution reduces to the statistics of the traces of powers of Haar unitaries, which are random unitary matrices drawn uniformly from the unitary group. For translation-invariant quadratic fermionic chains with interactions extending to $m$ neighbors and periodic boundary conditions, the Loschmidt amplitude admits a unitary matrix model / Toeplitz representation, which yields a work variable of the form $W=\sum_{r\le m} a_r \Re\operatorname{Tr} U^r$ (and in models with pairing terms -superconducting pairing- additional $b_r \Im\operatorname{Tr} U^r$ terms appear). By invoking multivariate central limit theorems for vectors of traces of unitaries, we obtain a Gaussian distribution for $P(W)$ with variance $\mathrm{Var}(W)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_r r (a_r^2+b_r^2)$ and asymptotic independence across different powers. We also characterise the conditions under which non-Gaussian tails arise, for example from many interaction terms or their slow decay, as well as the appearance of Fisher-Hartwig singularities. We illustrate these mechanisms in the XY chain. Various numerical diagnostics support the analytical results.

items.title: Correlative Microstructural Analysis of a Weathered Nantan Meteorite Fragment
items.summary: The weathering of iron-rich phases within meteorites is a multi-stage process that significantly alters the microstructure and chemical composition based both on the environmental condition at the location of landing and the exposure time since the fall. This work investigates the resulting phases of this process in a correlative and comparative manner using a naturally weathered Nantan meteorite fragment. Techniques including X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS), and X-ray Fluorescence Spectroscopy (XRF) were used for chemical and compositional determination and X-ray Diffraction (XRD) and Electron Backscatter Diffraction (EBSD) for phase determination and microstructural analysis. The combination of these techniques revealed the meteorite matrix to be predominantly composed of magnetite, with goethite and maghemite present as secondary phases. The meteorite had two pairs of distinct regions, one separated by Ni content and the other by grain size and Cl distribution. The Ni content regions are believed to have formed from a former Widmanstätten pattern, with the high ($\geq$2.6 at%) and low ($\leq$0.9 at%) Ni regions from plessite and kamacite, respectively. The kamacite and taenite within the plessite are suggested to have weathered through distinct mechanisms. The grain size regions were separated by a visible boundary 100-200 $μ$m wide where grains transitioned rapidly from fine to elongated grains and the Cl content changed from low and dispersed to concentrated spots. Lastly, a brecciated phase was found within the sample and was identified as a large cohenite grain which exhibited signs of weathering, including vein-like extensions of the matrix composed of NiO and magnetite, and deposits of iron and nickel carbonates.

items.title: Geometry-Encoded Hidden Orientational Memory
items.summary: Materials usually remember their past through dissipative changes of structure or through a net order. Simulations of caged colloidal ellipsoids at a fluid interface reveal a purely orientational memory. The particles stay in place, the layer has no net alignment, and a pattern written by a field is retained by capillary interactions between neighbors. It lasts hundreds of times longer than a particle takes to reorient, while every particle keeps rotating. The layer also remembers sequence: when two strong fields act one after the other on the same particles, it records which came last.

items.title: Viscous hydrodynamics from correlated losses
items.summary: Interactions turn a gas into a fluid. We show that two-body loss can take their place. Correlated loss induces elastic scattering, as required by the optical theorem, which dominates at strong loss via the quantum Zeno effect. A nondegenerate gas with only two-body loss thus flows hydrodynamically, with viscosity and thermal conductivity close to those of the unitary Fermi gas. As loss heats the gas, both grow in time with a universal exponent 3/8. Unlike single-particle loss, two-body loss can engineer collisions, and hence transport, in quantum matter.

items.title: Cooperative Boundary Switching of Mesoscopic Real Spectra in a Non-Hermitian Chain Family
items.summary: At fixed bulk criticality, every fixed nonsingular real single-end potential preserves a growing local population of real eigenvalues in an open analytic family of non-Hermitian chains. An open region of two-end real potentials removes this population. A boundary-amplitude criterion fixes the minimum number of controlled ends. The population grows as $\sqrt N$, where $N$ is chain length, although its normalized spectral weight vanishes and the local limiting bands remain unchanged. For a representative chain's four zero-detuning settings, an independent passive Hermitian double chain converts this distinction into separated resonances at one fixed local port under a common coupling scan at fixed probe carrier. Its absolute reflection contrast and stability margin both scale as $N^{-1}$, with explicit sufficient resource budgets. Boundary amplitudes thus fix a minimum control requirement that limiting bands and thermodynamic spectral density do not specify.

items.title: A Conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes Formulation for PHREEQC-Coupled Reactive Transport with Cell-Based Surface Complexation
items.summary: We present a mass-conservative Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes (DBS) formulation for reactive transport with cell-based surface complexation in image-based porous media, coupled to PHREEQC and implemented in GeoChemFoam, an OpenFOAM-based toolbox. Dissolved species are transported in the physical mobile-water fraction, adsorbed species are stored as conservative cell-scale surface inventories, and each reactive cell is coupled to PHREEQC. Reactive surface area is prescribed independently as a cell field, so that internal area left unresolved by segmentation of microporous phases can be represented while DBS flow and transport are retained in the resolved pore space. The implementation is verified with a test suite that isolates the coupling of transport and chemistry from the construction of reactive surface area. Aqueous and adsorbed mass balance is evaluated against a one-dimensional analytical retardation benchmark and closed-system batch calculations. The smooth-interface surface-area algorithms are tested on idealised two- and three-dimensional geometries. In a two-scale lithium micromodel, DBS reproduces fully resolved aqueous and sorbed inventories within 0.6% across Pe=0.1-10. The applications comprise Pb2+ retardation by hydrous ferric oxide coatings in a two-dimensional fracture network, competitive Mn2+/Mg2+ exchange in a three-dimensional Kelvin-cell sorbent, and Sr2+/Ca2+ exchange in Estaillades limestone.
