In the fracture-network and limestone cases, the formulation yields spatially resolved aqueous and adsorbed inventories even where reactive surface area is only partly resolved at the image scale. The framework therefore supports conservative surface-complexation modelling in both resolved and unresolved pore structures, with relevance to contaminant retention, selective ion capture, and radionuclide transport.

items.title: Retraction of a liquid drop in a Hele-Shaw cell
items.summary: When a long liquid drop is confined in a Hele-Shaw cell, the pull of surface tension produces a rapid retraction of its tip, causing it to bulge out as it draws up the excess liquid. Using numerical simulations, we demonstrate that this retraction is self-similar at long times, with the speed of retraction slowing like $t^{-1/2}$, where $t$ is the duration of retraction. After showing how this scaling can be understood using force and mass balance, we perform an asymptotic analysis of the Hele-Shaw equations to derive both the shape of the retracting drop, as well as prefactors of the scaling laws. Excellent agreement is found between our simulations and theory, and the experimental consequences are pointed out.

items.title: Topological superconductivity in layered d-wave altermagnetic metals
items.summary: We investigate multilayer d-wave altermagnetic metals with odd-parity helical p-wave pairing. In the minimal bilayer system, interlayer tunneling reconstructs the spin-split Fermi surfaces and generates two layer-hybridized sectors with distinct effective chemical potentials. Without Rashba spin-orbit coupling (RSOC), the emergent mirror symmetry and subsystem chiral symmetry stabilize phases with different numbers of helical Majorana edge-mode pairs and additional counterpropagating pairs, jointly characterized by the mirror Chern number and the winding numbers defined along high-symmetry lines. The combination of RSOC and the altermagnetic exchange field gaps out the helical Majorana pairs while, in a certain parameter regime, leaving another pair of counterpropagating Majorana edge modes gapless, giving rise to second-order topological phases with isolated or twofold Majorana corner modes, as well as a hybrid-order phase in which gapless Majorana edge modes coexist with Majorana corner modes. We identify a layer symmetry that elucidates the physical origin of these phases. For an arbitrary N-layer system, such a symmetry naturally arises from the interlayer-coupling matrix, allowing N-fold Majorana corner modes to emerge when all layer-hybridized sectors enter the nontrivial second-order regime. Our results establish the interplay among the layer degree of freedom, odd-parity pairing, and Fermi-surface configurations as a controllable route to engineering topological superconductivity in layered altermagnetic systems.

items.title: Nanoscale Mapping of Strain-engineered Excitons in Monolayer WSe$_2$
items.summary: Excitons in monolayer transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) are highly sensitive to external stimuli, allowing control of resonance energies and lifetimes through electric and magnetic fields, heterostructures, moire potentials and mechanical strain. Observations of single-photon emission (SPE) near sample edges, wrinkles, and strained nanobubbles have motivated strain-engineering aimed at realizing localized emitters in 2D materials. The origin of these emitters remains unclear and prior studies have relied on far-field spectroscopy with strain profiles inferred separately through topography, limiting direct correlation between local strain and excitonic response. We directly probe strain-modified excitonic spectra in monolayer WSe$_2$ using cryogenic scattering-type scanning near-field optical microscopy (s-SNOM). We compare two strain-engineering techniques, nano-indentation and patterned substrates, used to produce SPEs. At 9 K, we spatially resolve exciton resonance shifts with sub-diffraction limit resolution, simultaneously measuring near-field optical response and topography. We observe that strain transferred from nano-indentation into a deformable polymer substrate differs from that produced by draping TMDs over patterned dielectric pillars. Adhesion and tearing during plastic deformation drive a compressive exciton blueshift, while draping produces dominant tensile strain. Comparing the strain model results to the experimentally observed energy shifts shows that the nano-indentation strain is over an order of magnitude smaller than previously inferred, due to puncturing of the fragile monolayer, whereas pillar-strained devices remain intact under more modest strain. These differences suggest SPE arises from complex, strain-mediated interactions rather than simple confinement potentials, establishing s-SNOM as a powerful probe of quantum emission in strained 2D materials.

items.title: Anomalies, higher symmetries, and homotopy theory I: crossed precosheaves and a nonabelian Cech construction
items.summary: Symmetries of a quantum field theory or a quantum lattice model are expected to be described not by a group but by a homotopy type, whose homotopy groups are the higher symmetry groups and whose Postnikov invariants encode 't Hooft anomalies. We propose a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies based on the structure of localized symmetries in the operator-algebraic approach. The input is a crossed precosheaf: a collection of groups attached to regions of space, equipped with pairings recording that the commutator of two transformations localized in two regions is localized in their intersection. To a crossed precosheaf and a finite family of regions we attach a pointed connected homotopy type, the Cech-Loday classifying space. As the family of regions ranges over finite covers of space, the classifying spaces form a pro-object in the homotopy category. There is a canonical map from the ordinary classifying space of the symmetry group to this pro-type. Composing this map with a group action gives an anomaly whose nontriviality obstructs gauging. In favorable cases, the Cech-Loday space is essentially independent of the cover. In such cases, the homotopy fiber of the canonical map is a candidate for the classifying space of the higher group of symmetries. We give examples of crossed precosheaves arising from gauge transformations in continuum field theory and from quantum cellular automata and finite-depth circuits. For quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions, our construction recovers the Else-Nayak index and its generalizations to two dimensions.

items.title: Fluctuation-driven multi-step charge density wave melting in monolayer TiSe$_2$
items.summary: The exact microscopic origin, symmetry, and thermal melting mechanism of the charge density wave (CDW) phase in TiSe$_2$ remain intensely debated, particularly regarding chiral structural order and multi-step phase transitions. Using large-scale molecular dynamics driven by an accurate machine-learning interatomic potential, we resolve the finite-temperature structural dynamics of the monolayer TiSe$_2$. We demonstrate that CDW melting deviates from conventional mean-field second-order behavior, undergoing a two-step process characterized by an extended fluctuation region ($200-250$ K) with proliferating domain walls, phase decoherence, component-selective melting, and an overdamped soft optical phonon. Furthermore, anisotropic long-wavelength thermal fluctuations spontaneously stabilize an asymmetric $3Q$ CDW order with $P1$ symmetry. These findings provide a unified microscopic framework for fluctuation-driven transitions in 2D quantum materials, demonstrating that the complex CDW physics of TiSe$_2$ is captured entirely via non-perturbative electron-phonon and phonon-phonon interactions.

items.title: Electron-Mediated Phonon Polaritons in Quantum Cavities
items.summary: Phonon-photon coupling in quantum materials is commonly treated as an effective direct interaction, neglecting the crucial role played by electrons. Here we develop a gauge-invariant theory of cavity phonon polaritons that captures electronic screening, dissipation, and hybridization. We show that screening can suppress polariton formation in metals, severely constraining cavity control of phonon-mediated superconductivity. By contrast, interband electronic resonances in time-reversal-symmetric gapped systems can strongly enhance phonon-photon coupling, enabling robust polariton formation down to the monolayer limit despite electronic absorption. We illustrate these effects in NbSe2, hBN, and gapped graphene. Finally, we show that gauge invariance enforces photon decoupling from a critical soft phonon, establishing a general no-go mechanism for photon condensation.

items.title: Full-Continuum Ultrafast Quantum Gas Microscopy
items.summary: Quantum gas microscopy provides single-shot access to many-body configurations, but their microscopic reconstruction has so far largely relied on a predefined discrete spatial basis during fluorescence readout. Here we realize ultrafast atom-resolved fluorescence microscopy of an ultracold $^{162}$Dy gas directly in continuous space, with all external confinement removed during imaging. Exploiting the large mass and broad optical transition of dysprosium together with a high numerical aperture in-vacuum objective, we detect single atoms within $4\,μ\mathrm{s}$ while maintaining an effective point-spread function with a full width at half maximum of $254.8(3)\,\mathrm{nm}$, and an isolated single-atom classification fidelity of $99.72(3)\%$. We use the measured single-atom response to construct a statistical configuration-inference model that recovers atomic positions and multiplicities, coming from overlapping atoms, directly from single fluorescence snapshots. Benchmarking our model on Monte-Carlo generated images shows a total reconstruction fidelity of $98.7\%$. Our approach extends quantum gas microscopy beyond predefined detection lattices, enabling atom-resolved measurements of counting statistics and higher-order spatial correlations directly on the intrinsic length scales of continuum many-body systems.

items.title: Instability of Markov chains under infinitesimal coherent dissipation
items.summary: Under local Lindbladian evolution, the growth of conditional mutual information and its associated Markov length scale is not limited by Lieb-Robinson bounds, yet it has been unclear how quickly the Markov length can increase. We show that an arbitrarily short, strictly local Lindbladian can generate infinite Markov length from a product state. We also construct strictly local Lindbladians that converge rapidly to steady states with algebraically decaying conditional mutual information. Despite their long-range conditional correlations, the states we construct are local reversibly connected to a product state by sublinear depth circuits. Thus infinite Markov length does not imply slow relaxation nor obstruct phase stability when suitably defined.

items.title: Transmission representation of the Josephson free energy beyond the short-junction limit
items.summary: Beenakker's formula, $U(\varphi)-U(0)=Δ\sum_n\bigl(1-\sqrt{1-τ_n\sin^2(\varphi/2)}\bigr)$, expresses the zero-temperature energy-phase relation of a short Josephson junction through its normal-state transmission eigenvalues. We generalize this transmission representation beyond the short-junction limit and express the phase-dependent free energy of a time-reversal-symmetric $s$-wave junction as a Matsubara sum over channels with frequency-dependent transmissions. The representation constrains the small-phase expansion of the free energy. In particular, we prove that the normalized ratio of its quartic and quadratic coefficients satisfies $-1\leα_r\le7/80$ at finite temperature. We also construct a four-site junction with $α_r>0$, which disproves the conjectured upper bound $α_r\le0$. So that these results can be trusted without repeating the derivations, every numbered equation is formally verified in the Lean proof assistant.

items.title: Programmable Polaron Models and Tomography in Trapped-Ion Quantum Simulators
items.summary: Strong coupling between mobile charge carriers or excitons and lattice vibrations gives rise to polarons: quasiparticles formed by charge carriers dressed by a cloud of phonon excitations. Polaron formation determines transport properties of systems ranging from transition-metal oxides and organic semiconductors to light-harvesting complexes. In excitonic systems that admit a hard-core boson description, mapping the excitations to pseudospins provides a natural framework for studying polaron physics, including the nonperturbative regime in which hopping amplitudes, phonon energies, and coupling strengths are comparable. Here, we propose a trapped-ion blueprint for realizing spin-phonon Hamiltonians with programmable spatial coupling between excitation density and phonon displacements, encompassing local Holstein and long-range Fröhlich-type interactions. To access strongly dressed quasiparticles whose bare spectral weight is suppressed, we introduce displaced Green's functions implemented through spin-dependent phonon displacements. Their spectral response reveals the polaron band spectrum, including binding energies and phonon-excitation sidebands, while spatially resolved measurements probe the structure of the phonon dressing cloud, providing a route to polaron tomography. We further complement this spectroscopy with direct and ancilla-assisted measurements of spin-phonon correlations that track the coupled dynamics of the excitation and its environment. These approaches connect the emergent quasiparticle spectrum to the microscopic buildup of its dressing cloud, enabling controlled studies of how the spatial range of coupling shapes polaron formation and mobility.

items.title: Non-Abelian quantum Hall states at strong Landau level mixing: finding anyons with first-principles AI
items.summary: Non-Abelian anyons, strange particles forming the basis of fault-tolerant topological quantum computing, are predicted to emerge in fractional quantum Hall states at even-denominator filling factors. Identifying which topological order is realized has proven to be a challenging problem that requires an accurate, non-perturbative treatment of realistic Landau level mixing, which has so far been missing from theoretical studies. Here we present the first complete solution of non-Abelian quantum Hall problem that includes all electrons and all Landau levels, for spin-polarized electrons at filling factor $ν= 3/2$. We develop a momentum-resolved neural-network variational wave function, optimized solely on the microscopic Hamiltonian, which gives direct access to the topologically degenerate ground states. Without any physics input about the expected outcome, it discovers a degenerate ground-state manifold whose entanglement reveals anyons with quantum dimension $\sqrt{2}$, the hallmark of Ising-type non-Abelian order. By directly computing the overlap with trial wave functions, we further show that Landau level mixing favors the anti-Pfaffian over other candidate states. Our results demonstrate the power of neural-network wave functions in finding and characterizing non-Abelian anyons from first principles, in regimes of strong Landau level mixing, relevant to many recent experiments.

items.title: Measurement-induced criticality for non-Abelian anyons: The monitored golden chain
items.summary: Non-Abelian anyon chains whose interactions favor a single fusion channel host quantum critical ground states described by minimal-model conformal field theories (CFTs) protected by a topological symmetry. We show that their measurement-only counterpart, where non-commuting fusion charge measurements act locally on the anyons of a chain of $L$ sites, provides a fundamental example of a non-unitary CFT controlling a non-Abelian learning problem. Mapping the monitored dynamics to a random tensor network, we numerically find $1/L$ scaling Lyapunov gaps, logarithmic entanglement scaling with the chord length, and an effective central charge in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record. The conserved topological charge sharpens with dynamical exponent $z= 1$ and is learnable by a decoder on an $O(L)$ time scale. As the topological symmetry is a non-invertible symmetry of the $SU(2)_k$ anyon theories, we establish the monitored golden chain $(k=3)$ as a non-Abelian generalization of the weakly (Kramers-Wannier) self-dual quantum critical point of the toric code $(k=2)$, and the first of a family for $k\geq 3$.

items.title: Optimal Disorder Strength for Approximate Unitary $k$-Designs in Spin Chains
items.summary: Quantum simulators with disordered spin Hamiltonians offer a natural route to Haar-like unitary ensembles, but face a competition. Disorder enhances randomness, yet strong disorder suppresses dynamics and localizes the system in the computational basis. This suggests an optimal intermediate disorder strength for approximating a unitary $k$-design, which has so far been identified mainly empirically. Here, we develop a perturbative theory for the moment gap $Δ^{(k)}$, the deviation of the $k$-th moment operator from its Haar value, for the full spectrum of the interacting XXZ chain in a fixed-magnetization sector. We find the non-monotonic asymptotic scalings $\ln Δ^{(k)}\sim -σ^2$ at weak disorder and $\ln Δ^{(k)}\sim -1/σ$ at strong disorder, whose crossover sets an optimal disorder strength $σ_c\sim J_{xy}$, where $J_{xy}$ is the energy scale of the non-random interaction. We further show that a multi-quench protocol further suppresses the gap exponentially in the number of quenches. Numerical simulations confirm both scalings and this exponential suppression, and we demonstrate the usefulness of the protocol for classical shadow tomography. This work suggests that strong disorder may block both thermalization and the formation of unitary designs through a common localization mechanism.

items.title: Invertible subalgebras for chiral semion topological order
items.summary: Chiral topological order is incompatible with strictly two-dimensional local commuting-projector Hamiltonians on finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Invertible subalgebras (ISAs) provide an alternative framework. We construct an ISA supporting chiral semions, together with its anti-semion commutant, on a square lattice with one qubit per edge. We give explicit non-Pauli generators for both algebras and prove that together they generate all local operators on the Hilbert space. Starting from the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ toric code, we condense the boson $e^2m^2$ and identify the semion and anti-semion algebras. We then decompose each $\mathbb{Z}_4$ qudit into two qubits and use a finite-depth circuit to disentangle one qubit per edge fixed by the condensation constraints. Pumping the semion ISA along the $z$ direction defines an explicit three-dimensional non-Clifford quantum cellular automaton (QCA). We show that pumping eight times is equivalent to a translation followed by a finite-depth quantum circuit with ancillary qubits. We also give an explicit finite-depth circuit relating this construction to the semion QCA previously obtained from topological quantum field theory. A similar condensation construction yields a $U(1)_4$ ISA on a square lattice. Together with the semion and earlier odd-prime ISAs, finite stacking realizes every pointed Witt class of bosonic Abelian anyon theories. Finally, we extend both constructions to all spatial dimensions $d=4k{-}2$, with one qubit or $\mathbb{Z}_4$ qudit on each $(2k{-}1)$-cell for the semion or $U(1)_4$ ISA, respectively.

items.title: A comparison between statistics and 't Hooft anomaly
items.summary: Anomalies of generalized symmetries are closely related to the statistics of topological excitations. Truncating a symmetry transformation to a finite region produces an operator that creates symmetry defects on its boundary; we call this a symmetry patch operator. Such operators resemble hopping operators that create topological excitations at the boundary of their support, but this geometric similarity does not justify identifying the two. For finite Abelian groups in one spatial dimension, we prove that if the same family of local operators defines both valid hopping operators and compatible symmetry patches, the type-III component of the anomaly is $-2$ times that of the statistics. We establish a one-to-one correspondence between statistics and anomaly by treating hopping operators as symmetric operators that commute with the global symmetry, following the description of symmetry through the algebra of local symmetric operators. We explain this correspondence through gauging by coupling boundary matter to a Dijkgraaf-Witten gauge field in one higher spatial dimension. Hopping operators act on the gauge-invariant degrees of freedom. After fixing the background gauge field, the residual gauge transformations become the global symmetry, and the gauge invariance of hopping operators becomes the requirement that they commute with this symmetry.

items.title: A hierarchy of exact lower bounds on the Laughlin spectral gap
items.summary: We develop a bootstrap approach to deriving lower bounds on the spectral gap of the first Haldane pseudopotential Hamiltonian on the sphere with $N_Φ$ flux quanta for arbitrary $N_Φ$, including in the thermodynamic limit $N_Φ\to \infty$. Our approach can in principle be generalized to pseudopotentials describing other model wavefunctions such as the Moore-Read state or Read-Rezayi sequence. Our approach is based on Knabe's observation that if $H$ is a Hamiltonian with ground state energy $0$ then the spectral gap is at least $ε> 0$ if and only if $H^2 \succeq εH$. To show this inequality, we split $H^2$ into two parts, one that can be analytically bounded and another that can be bounded using a finite semidefinite program (SDP). Crucially, the size of this program is determined only by cutoff parameters, and the program depends on $N_Φ$ only parametrically, allowing us to obtain numerically exact (up to solver precision) lower bounds on the gap. In order to turn these numerical bounds into mathematically rigorous bounds, we introduce an algorithm that can produce nearly-optimal exact feasible points for large rational SDPs. We additionally provide an algorithm that establishes the rank stability of the semidefinite program in the limit $N_Φ\to \infty$ which is needed to certify the bound in the thermodynamic limit. Beyond establishing the Laughlin gap and revealing a potential method for deriving spectral gap lower bounds for other pseudopotentials, our work provides a general method for turning numerical semidefinite programming bounds into rigorous mathematical proofs, which may have wide applicability.

items.title: Fingerprints of an Imbert-Fedorov-like effect in the tunneling transmission of Rarita-Schwinger semi-metals
items.summary: We study tunneling through a square barrier in a rotationally symmetric Rarita-Schwinger semi-metal and identify fingerprints of an Imbert-Fedorov-like effect in the tunneling transmission. The problem is intrinsically multichannel at all energies because there exist two propagating sectors with spin projections $m=1/2$ and $m=3/2$. We derive the transmission amplitudes analytically and compare the single-channel and coherent mixed-incidence cases in the two channels. Interestingly, we observe that tunneling at high energy shows a bias towards scattering into spin projection $3/2$ contributions. For single-channel injection, we find that the transmission remains symmetric under a mirror transformation of the incident angle. In contrast, for the coherent superposition, we find a directional asymmetry in the transmission probability $T(k_y)\neq T(-k_y)$. Importantly, this effect does not originate from an anisotropy of the dispersion. Instead, it arises from the phase structure of the multicomponent scattering states. The two spin projection sectors exhibit different scattering and barrier-propagation phases, which enter as interference terms when both channels appear as a coherent superposition. This interference term is identified as the cause of the broken mirror symmetry. We therefore discover an analog of the Imbert-Fedorov effect, at the level of interface-induced phase differences between internal wave components. Our result demonstrates that asymmetric tunneling can already occur in transport experiments, even in an idealized, isotropic multiband system, and should therefore not be automatically attributed solely to explicit band anisotropy.

items.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
items.summary: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. At v = 1/3 and 2/3, we observe backscattering resonances with three times the frequency, consistent with resonant transmission of e/3 charges via a single anyon transistor. We demonstrate controlled depletion to the last quasiparticle to form a single anyon quantum dot. Tracing the charge addition spectrum for quasiparticle number Nqp = 1-5, we observe highly irregular addition energies, consistent with DMRG modeling showing a complex orbital shell-filling behavior. At higher Nqp = 10-20, the addition energies show a striking pattern: quasiholes at 1/3 (and quasiparticles at 2/3) show a regular addition spectrum while quasiparticles at 1/3 (and quasiholes at 2/3) do not. We trace the origin of this irregularity to an attractive component of the inter-anyon interaction: by experimentally tuning the confining energy, we observe complete suppression of alternating charge sectors, after which the dot charges in increments of twice the fundamental charge. This observation indicates the emergence of an anyon binding energy as large as the charging energy.

items.title: Towards synergy between theory and experiments: First-passage processes under resetting with stochastic return protocols
items.summary: Stochastic resetting with stochastic return (SR) has recently emerged as an effective and practically relevant strategy for controlling first-passage phenomena and optimizing search processes by significantly reducing completion times in a wide class of stochastic systems. While most theoretical studies assume instantaneous return (IR), in realistic systems the return to the resetting position typically occurs over a finite time. We consider a 1-d diffusing particle in a harmonic trap with stiffnesses $k_1$ and $k_2$ during search and return, respectively. The particle searches for the target and, upon resetting at rate $r$, enters the return phase, continuing until it reaches either the origin or the absorbing target at $L>0$. Notably, the model permits target detection throughout the return phase, distinguishing it from IR scenarios. We analytically derive the MFPT for our model and determine parameter regions where SR enhances or suppresses search efficiency over the underlying dynamics, constructing the corresponding phase diagram using the coefficient of variation criterion. We further identify regimes in which SR is more efficient than IR using the SR criterion. This behavior is tested across different parameter sets taken from experimental studies by Goerlich et al., Biroli et al., and Besga et al. We map the parameter values reported in existing experimental studies onto our theoretical phase diagram, thereby identifying the regimes in which SR outperforms IR. In particular, we find that the most relevant region of the phase space, where SR is most beneficial corresponds to larger values of the potential strength in the search phase and lower values of potential in the return phase. Our results provide experimentally testable predictions and bridge the gap between theoretical resetting models and optical trap mediated finite-time return dynamics.

items.title: Spin textures at the Fermi surface of ferromagnets and associated torque
items.summary: We establish theoretically that transverse spin textures are generically induced by the spin-orbit interaction at the Fermi surface of centrosymmetric ferromagnetic metals. We confirm this prediction with {\em ab initio} computations for Fe, Co and Ni. By symmetry, this cannot be associated with spin-orbit torques under a uniform current. However, a new {\em current-gradient-induced} torque emerges in nanoscale geometries. For a series of Ni-based bilayers, the computed Ni thickness dependence of the current-gradient-induced torque is in quantitative agreement with measurements previously attributed to orbital torques. We discuss how this opens a new avenue for the electrical control of magnetic orders, possibly also including the Néel vector of metallic altermagnets.

items.title: Geometry-Enforced Topological Chiral Fermions in Amorphous Chiral Metals
items.summary: Since the prediction and observation of topological Weyl semimetals (chiral TSMs), there have been enormous efforts to characterize further condensed matter realizations of chiral fermions. These efforts were dramatically accelerated by the subsequent discovery of a profound link between low-energy topological and lattice chirality in structurally chiral crystals. Though TSMs are well understood in the limit of perfect translation symmetry, real solid-state materials host defects and disorder, and may even be rendered amorphous down to all but the smallest system length scales. Previous theoretical studies have concluded that chiral TSMs transition into trivial diffusive metals at moderate disorder scales, raising concerns that chiral TSM states may only be accessible in highly crystalline samples. In this work, we in contrast identify large families of chiral TSMs that instead persist under strong structural disorder even into the amorphous regime. We show that amorphous chiral TSM phases can be stabilized in particular by the presence of long-range order in the local structural chirality. We present extensive analytic and numerical calculations demonstrating the existence of both Weyl and higher-charge chiral fermions in amorphous metals whose topology and spin and orbital angular momentum textures are tunable via the interplay of average symmetry and geometry. To distinguish and generate new realizations of strongly disordered chiral fermions, we introduce an analytic approach grounded in symmetry group theory. We then introduce an amorphous Wilson loop numerical method to identify chiral fermions in metals with 3D structural disorder. Our findings bridge the crystalline and strongly disordered regimes of chiral TSMs, and indicate a clear route toward engineering geometry-enforced topology in noncrystalline materials and metamaterials.

items.title: Fluctuation-dissipation structure of quantum geometry
items.summary: Geometry of quantum states is a fundamental research area with applications ranging from topological materials in condensed matter to variational algorithms in quantum information. Due to their relative simplicity, pure states are often studied, while mixed states are generally needed, for instance to have nonzero temperatures or other statistical mixtures. Mixed-state geometry, however, is much more challenging and has so far lacked any overall structure that relates distance and curvature, like the Kähler structure does for pure states. This work introduces that missing structure. We show that it has the physical meaning of fluctuation-dissipation---by identifying distance with fluctuations and curvature with linear response---and becomes the known structure for pure states, but is non-Kähler otherwise. This paints a simple picture that unifies fluctuation-dissipation and geometry of quantum states. It also applies on parameter spaces, as encountered in condensed matter or estimation theory. Our picture implies that the geometry contains all linear responses and fluctuations, proves the usual fluctuation-dissipation relation, explains that quantum geometry is present in any sum rule, and allows one to geometrically characterize generic transport behaviors.

items.title: Finite temperature Fredholm determinants for dynamical correlation functions
items.summary: We study the long-time, large-distance asymptotics of finite-temperature dynamical Fredholm determinants using effective form factors. The method expresses these asymptotics as a functional of an effective phase shift. We determine its two branches on either side of a quadratic stationary point and the transition profile joining them. The profile is expressed through parabolic-cylinder functions. Its connection to the high-temperature Gaussian $β$ ensemble fixes the finite normalization, in agreement with an independent Riemann--Hilbert analysis. We also show that the leading exponential asymptotics suffice to recover the Euler-scale prediction of generalized hydrodynamics for the dynamical structure factor of hard rods.

items.title: Competing delocalisation and localisation induced by the dipolar tail in fragmented lattice gases
items.summary: We investigate how the long-range tail of dipole-dipole interactions modifies the dynamics of strongly interacting hard-core bosons in a one-dimensional lattice. In the nearest-neighbour model, large interactions generate an emergent Hilbert-space fragmentation into manifolds labelled by the number of nearest-neighbour bonds \(N_{\mathrm{NN}}\). The dipolar tail has a non-monotonic effect on this fragmented dynamics as the interaction-to-tunnelling ratio \(V/t\) is increased. At intermediate \(V/t\), it enhances delocalisation relative to the nearest-neighbour model by reducing the energetic detuning between neighbouring \(N_{\mathrm{NN}}\) manifolds and sustaining their hybridisation by hopping. At larger \(V/t\), the same tail lifts degeneracies within each manifold, beginning with the splitting associated with the next-nearest-neighbour bond number \(N_{\mathrm{NNN}}\), and promotes intra-manifold localisation and Hilbert-space shattering. The competition between these two effects produces a crossover from a delocalising to a localising role of the dipolar tail, visible in the late-time spatial inhomogeneity. This crossover occurs for nearly all initial states considered and persists at different fillings. Transverse confinement strengthens the short-range part of the dipolar tail and shifts the crossover to lower \(V/t\), bringing it into the regime relevant to current experiments with magnetic atoms and polar molecules.

items.title: Emergent Loop Geometry in Gauge-Equivariant Graph Neural Networks
items.summary: Gauge-equivariant graph neural networks generate ordered products of gauge links through local message passing, but the geometry of these internal structures is not captured by the receptive field alone. We investigate the statistical ensemble of closed lattice walks generated by recursive node- and edge-feature operations, independently of network training. Analytical and numerical results reveal a separation between rapid growth of contour length and much slower spatial expansion: deeper compositions generate increasingly long paths through repeated traversal of relatively compact regions. Loop expansions of fermionic observables provide a physical interpretation of this hierarchy, showing how spatial locality remains compatible with high-order dependence on nearby gauge fields. These findings identify complementary roles of network depth in extending spatial reach and enriching the representations constructed within that reach, providing a geometrical perspective on learning lattice gauge observables.

items.title: A thermodynamic analysis of nonsecular master equations, beyond strict energy conservation and Gibbs equilibrium state
items.summary: We present a systematic thermodynamic analysis of nonsecular GKLS master equations. When some energy transitions in the system are comparable with the dissipative rate, the secular approximation is not valid, and the positivity of the dynamics must be ensured via other approximations. The dynamics then presents features reminiscent from strong coupling to the environment: e.g. the equilibrium state with an environment at thermal equilibrium is not a Gibbs state of the local system Hamiltonian and the dynamics couples energy coherences and populations. Nonetheless, we build a unified, consistent thermodynamic framework for those dynamics. We focus on two approximations beyond the full secular approximation (the local and the more accurate geometric-arithmetic approximations), and then employ systematic perturbation theory on microscopic expressions for the first and second law of thermodynamics which relate irreversibility to the increase of system-environment correlations. We show that, in spite of the weak system-bath coupling, the system-bath interaction energy participates to the energy balance, and is directly linked to the Lamb-shift Hamiltonian. We compare this microscopic entropy production with the definition based on the contractivity of the reduced system dynamics (Spohn inequality). We show that, unlike for secular master equations, the two entropy production rates differ because of the presence of non-vanishing stationary coherences in the energy eigenbasis. However, in the case of a single thermal bath, the difference is purely transient, and no work can be cyclically extracted from the steady-state despite its non-Gibbs form. Finally, we illustrate our results with simple examples, clarifying and completing the thermodynamic picture of Markovian dynamics in the quantum regime.

items.title: Superexchange coupling between a dilute Gd3+ probe and orphan spins in a valence-bond glass
items.summary: The valence-bond-glass state of the 4d^1 double perovskite Ba2YMoO6 combines Mo^5+ singlets with residual paramagnetic "orphan" spins whose coupling is hard to reach with bulk probes. We probe them by electron paramagnetic resonance of a dilute Gd^3+ ion on the Y^3+ site via broadband coplanar-waveguide transmission at 5 K. The isostructural nonmagnetic niobate Ba2YNbO6, doped with the same Gd^3+ probe, is a fixed-lattice control. The Gd^3+ linewidth nearly doubles in the magnetic host. Dipolar coupling to the sparse orphans is nearly an order of magnitude too weak; the excess is instead reproduced by a transferred f-d superexchange of J ~ 0.2 K, so the width is a static measure of orphan-spin coupling. The half-field (Delta m_S = +/-2) satellite collapses in the magnetic host, a dynamical dephasing channel, while the unchanged g-factor marks a zero-mean random internal field. Together the two channels probe the coupling and dynamics of valence-bond-glass orphan spins.

items.title: Extreme Suppression of Thermal Conductivity in Monolayer Beryllene
items.summary: We demonstrate an extreme suppression of thermal conductivity in monolayer beryllene through first-principles solutions of the phonon Boltzmann transport equation. While the fully converged three-phonon calculation predicts a room-temperature lattice thermal conductivity of 154.3 W/(m$\cdot$K), inclusion of four-phonon interactions suppresses it to 10.7 W/(m$\cdot$K), a reduction of more than 90\%. This exceptionally large reduction of the thermal conductivity is amongst the highest reported in two-dimensional materials. The microscopic origin of this breakdown is traced to the strong sensitivity of the low-frequency flexural ZA phonons to four-phonon scattering: mode-resolved scattering rates reveal a pronounced enhancement of ZA scattering, which substantially shortens their lifetimes and suppresses their dominant contribution to heat conduction. Moreover, the temperature dependence of the thermal conductivity changes from $κ\propto T^{-0.86}$ to $κ\propto T^{-1.38}$ upon inclusion of four-phonon processes. Our results establish $α$-beryllene as an unusually strong case of four-phonon-controlled thermal transport amongst two-dimensional materials. These findings identify selective higher-order scattering of flexural phonons as a key mechanism for controlling thermal transport in strongly anharmonic low-dimensional systems.

items.title: Explicitly correlated ground states with a feedback-free variational hybrid algorithm
items.summary: Explicitly correlated methods, which represent dominant short-range correlations by a diagonal Jastrow-type correlator, are designed to accurately describe systems of strongly correlated electrons, such as the fully periodic 2D Fermi--Hubbard model. However, as the reference state is compact in momentum space whereas the correlator acts naturally in real space, there is a fundamental mismatch of bases that classical algorithms resolve only by restricting the reference or the correlator. Here we propose a hybrid algorithm in which a quantum processor prepares a low-entanglement momentum-space matrix product state (MPS), precomputed classically by the transcorrelated method at the cost of a nonvariational energy, rotates it to real space, and measures in bases fixed by the Hamiltonian. Because the measurement bases are independent of the correlator, the correlator can be variationally optimized entirely in classical post-processing with no quantum-classical feedback loop. We demonstrate our algorithm on 32 qubits of Quantinuum's H2-2 with a bond-dimension-4 MPS for the half-filled $4 \times 4$ lattice and achieve a relative ground-state energy error of $16 \pm 4\%$ after postselection, reduced to $3.5 \pm 0.5\%$ by calibration using low-order moments from the MPS. Compared with other feedback-free hybrid algorithms, even under generous assumptions, our method requires fewer samples than quantum-selected configuration interaction and fewer two-qubit gates than quantum Krylov methods.

items.title: Entanglement in the $θ$-vacuum
items.summary: We compute the entanglement entropy and the entanglement spectrum of the vacuum state in the massive Schwinger model at a finite $θ$ angle. By computing two-point correlation functions we show that the correlation length diverges in the critical region. We clarify the physical origin of entanglement entropy enhancement at $θ=π$ by relating it to the competition between distinct electric-flux vacuum branches. We show that the peak near $θ=π$ persists across the range of masses studied and corresponds to the point of maximal competition between distinct vacuum branches with opposite electric-field orientation, where quantum fluctuations due to fermion pair creation are maximized. While this entropy enhancement is generic, a pronounced compression of the low-lying entanglement spectrum at $θ=π$ distinguishes the near-critical case ($m/g\simeq0.33$). Using the Bisognano--Wichmann (BW) theorem, we construct a lattice BW entanglement Hamiltonian and compare it with the exact modular Hamiltonian obtained from the reduced density matrix. We observe agreement in the infrared sector, indicating that the entanglement Hamiltonian is well approximated by a spatially weighted Hamiltonian. Finally, we discuss possible applications to entanglement in topological insulators and quantum wires. In this work, we used the chirally rotated formulation of the Schwinger model Hamiltonian. We identify an additive vacuum-energy artifact induced by the discretization of the chirally rotated lattice and derive its exact free-lattice form to subtract it in the continuum limit.

items.title: Visualizing Chiral Edge Modes in Twisted Cuprate Superconductors via Scanning-Probe Quantum Sensing
items.summary: Recently, unconventional superconductivity hosted by twisted van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures has received immense interest due to the exotic pairing symmetry, electronic interactions and nontrivial topological nature that are naturally relevant to the fast-advancing quantum technologies. Here, we report scanning-probe quantum sensing of nanoscale electromagnetic behaviors of twisted vdW cuprate superconductors. Using single-spin relaxometry, we directly visualize edge modes spontaneously formed in twisted Bi2Sr2CaCu2O8+x (BSCCO). By investigating temperature dependent variations of edge-state-induced quantum spin relaxation, we experimentally evaluate the magnitude of nontrivial topological band gap opened at nodal points in twisted BSCCO and its critical temperature behaviors under different twist angles. We further observe alternating chiral domains defined by edge modes, exploring experimental signatures of in-plane magnetic field-induced topology in 45° twisted BSCCO. Our results advance the current understanding of twisted vdW nodal superconductors, presenting an appealing high-temperature topological superconducting material platform for cutting-edge quantum innovation.

items.title: Composition-controlled optical fingerprints and anisotropy of self-trapped excitons in double perovskites
items.summary: Double perovskites (DPs) offer a compositionally versatile platform for photocatalysis and optoelectronics, but their soft lattices favor strong exciton-phonon coupling and self-trapped excitons (STEs), which produce broad, red-shifted photoluminescence (PL). Here, we combine optical spectroscopy and ab initio calculations to study lead-free, Sb-doped Cs2BInCl6 nanocrystals with B-site alloying from Na to K. Alloying tunes the PL energy from about 2.48 to 2.70 eV, while absorption features near 3.8 eV remain nearly unchanged. Calculations reveal that Sb doping enables bright radiative recombination channels and delocalizes the excitonic wavefunction. We identify STEs responsible for the large PL red shift, associated with an upward shift of dopant-hybridized in-gap states. Na-to-K substitution selectively changes the STE lattice distortion, explaining why PL varies strongly with composition while absorption does not. Theory further predicts pronounced PL polarization anisotropy that reflects the STE wavefunction's spatial structure and depends on B-site composition. Time-resolved anisotropy measurements closely agree with these predictions, providing experimental fingerprints of the excitonic wavefunction and its evolution with alloying. Together, these results disentangle the roles of doping and alloying in lead-free DPs and establish polarization-resolved spectroscopy as a probe of STE wavefunctions.

items.title: Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System for extrapolative prediction of perovskite solar cells
items.summary: Existing machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells struggle to predict devices made from new materials. Most treat device layers as arbitrary categorical labels and represent perovskite absorbers either through featureless composition vectors or through rigid crystal graphs that require a pre-solved unit cell. As a result, they cannot generalize to unrecorded alloys or unfamiliar cell architectures. We present the Virtual-Alloy Physics-Aware Semantic System (V-PaSS), an architecture built around the physical continuity of perovskite solid solutions. V-PaSS represents arbitrary mixed-cation, mixed-halide absorbers by interpolating relaxed crystal graphs of 23 pure $ABX_3$ endpoint compounds via Vegard's law with learned bandgap bowing. For the device stack, it couples layer sequence and cell polarity (n-i-p or p-i-n) with interfacial band offsets and encodes chemical descriptions with a scientific language model. Evaluated under an institution-grouped protocol where test devices come exclusively from unseen laboratories, an untuned default configuration of V-PaSS achieves the lowest error among fourteen tested models (2.861% MAE, a 5.2% relative reduction over a gradient-boosted baseline at 3.017%, and outperforming the best tuned benchmark at 2.912%). V-PaSS pulls furthest ahead where test devices differ most from training: reducing error by 15.7-19.0% on unseen absorber alloys, by 16.1% on mixed absorbers from new laboratories, and widening its lead over the baseline by 3.6$\times$ on devices with unobserved transport layers. Combined with tree ensembles, V-PaSS sets a new state of the art across all five benchmark splits.

items.title: Dark state preparation in a zero-field-split molecular triplet
items.summary: We propose a protocol to prepare and probe dark states in a single-molecule electron spin resonance based on atomic force microscopy (ESR-AFM), thus extending existing techniques developed to address Rabi oscillations. To this end, we simulate in analogy to atomic physics the coherent manipulation of a three-level system in the V-configuration using a multifrequency magnetic field. More specifically, we consider a neutral molecule with a zero-field-split (ZFS) first excited triplet and analyze within a pump-probe scheme the dynamics of the total triplet population. In the triplet subspace, the dark state is a coherent superposition formed by two ZFS states which does not evolve in time despite a continuous resonant driving towards the third one. We characterize the properties of this state comparing it to its fully incoherent counterpart. Within a density-matrix formalism for open systems, we then compute the expected dark state signatures both for ideal scenarios and for the realistic parameterization of ESR-AFM on pentacene.

items.title: Extending the mean first-passage-time formalism to the reconstruction of high free-energy barriers: A top-start approach
items.summary: Rare events, such as crystal nucleation in mildly supercooled liquids, are characterized by waiting times that can be much longer than the timescale of the underlying microscopic dynamics. The mean first-passage time (MFPT) formalism [J. Wedekind and D. Reguera, J. Phys. Chem. B 112, 11060 (2008)] provides a route to reconstruct one-dimensional free-energy profiles from the MFPT and steady-state distribution measured along a reaction coordinate, but conventional implementations become inefficient for sufficiently high barriers because spontaneous crossings are rarely observed. We introduce a "top-start" extension that initiates trajectories near the barrier top and reconstructs the free-energy profile from their subsequent evolution away from the barrier toward lower-free-energy regions. We establish the equivalence between the top-start and two-region constructions using a Markov-chain transition-matrix formulation. We validate the method using one-dimensional random-walk simulations across low, medium, and high free-energy barriers, with transition-matrix calculations providing an exact benchmark for the corresponding discretized models. The top-start reconstruction remains accurate in the high-barrier regime where conventional MFPT sampling becomes prohibitively inefficient.

items.title: Momentum conservation for ab initio calculations with pseudopotentials via a phase space electronic structure formulation
items.summary: We demonstrate how to build a robust phase space electronic Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_\text{PS}(\boldsymbol{R},\boldsymbol{P})$ that depends on nuclear position $\boldsymbol{R}$ and nuclear momentum $\boldsymbol{P}$ in the presence of ionic pseudopotentials. In particular, we show that in order to account for the non-local component of a pseudopotential while also conserving linear and angular momentum, one is forced to introduce a non-local one-electron operator $\hat{\boldsymbolΓ}^\text{nl}$ that couples electronic and nuclear momenta together. To test the validity of our ansatz, we derive a generalized form of Nafie's exact equality (which relates electronic momentum and electronic position) so as to include the presence of pseudopotentials. We then benchmark our proposed phase space electronic structure theory against this generalized Nafie-like result for a diverse set of diatomic molecules spanning a wide range of elements. We find excellent agreement across this ab initio test set, highlighting the strength of our method in capturing meaningful electronic momentum beyond the Born-Oppenheimer framework.

items.title: Plasmon modes in triple-point semimetal, its quadratic cousin, and Hopf semimetal
items.summary: We study collective charge excitations in pseudospin-1 triple-point semimetals within the random-phase approximation, considering both the linearised model with a flat-band and its quadratic-corrected counterpart. We analyse their density response, Drude weights, screening, plasmon dispersion and damping, particle-hole continua, and Friedel oscillations from the long-wavelength to the arbitrary-momentum regime. The quadratic correction renders the flat-band dispersive and endows it with a Fermi surface, thereby affecting the overall response. Comparisons with Weyl and Hopf semimetals reveal how bandstructure and quantum geometry jointly govern collective charge dynamics. While the Drude weights are determined by the Fermi surface and band-velocities, interband screening, plasmon dispersion, and Friedel oscillations reflect the quantum geometry of the eigenstates.

items.title: Converting long-range entanglement into mixture: tensor-network approach to local equilibration
items.summary: In the out-of-equilibrium evolution induced by a quench, fast degrees of freedom generate long-range entanglement that is hard to encode with standard tensor networks. However, local observables only sense such long-range correlations through their contribution to the reduced local state as a mixture. We present a tensor network method that identifies such long-range entanglement and efficiently transforms it into mixture, much easier to represent. In this way, we obtain an effective description of the time-evolved state as a density matrix that captures the long-time behavior of local operators with finite computational resources.

items.title: Exact Microscopic One-Body Reduction in the Symmetric Exclusion Process
items.summary: The symmetric exclusion process (SEP) is a paradigmatic model of interacting particle transport. Its current--density correlations are governed by an infinite many-body hierarchy of equations. Only recently, this hierarchy was found to collapse at large scales onto a single closed equation. Is this remarkable simplification created by coarse graining, or does it reflect a deeper property already present in the microscopic dynamics? Here we show that the second scenario is realized. At arbitrary time on the lattice, the entire hierarchy collapses onto a single linear equation which is exactly equivalent to a persistence problem for a single auxiliary random walker. Thus an interacting many-body problem reduces exactly to a genuine one-body problem before any scaling limit is taken. This reduction determines the complete finite-time correlation profile, including during nonequilibrium relaxation. More broadly, the microscopic operator uncovered here opens a route to more general correlation functions in the SEP, and may point to a general organizing principle for nonequilibrium interacting particle systems.

items.title: Symmetry defects and gauging for quantum states with matrix product unitary symmetries
items.summary: In this work, we examine the consequences of the existence of a finite group of matrix product unitary (MPU) symmetries for matrix product states (MPS). We generalize the well-understood picture of onsite unitary symmetries, which give rise to virtual symmetry defects given by insertions of operators in the bonds of the MPS. In the MPU case, we can define analogous defect tensors, this time sitting on lattice sites, that can be created, moved, and fused by local unitary operators. We leverage this formalism to study the gauging of MPU symmetries. We introduce a condition, block independence, under which we can gauge the symmetries by promoting the symmetry defects to gauge degrees of freedom, yielding an MPS of the same bond dimension that supports a local version of the symmetry given by commuting gauge constraints. Whenever block independence does not hold (which happens, in particular, whenever the symmetry representation is anomalous), a modification of our method which we call state-level gauging still gives rise to a locally symmetric MPS by promotion of the symmetry defects, at the expense of producing gauge constraints that do not commute on different sites.

items.title: Time-Resolved Phonon Dispersions of Thermally Excited Graphite at the Nanoscale
items.summary: Lattice vibrations govern the propagation of heat in materials, and investigating their dynamics through time-resolved phonon dispersion measurements would provide insight into these excitations and their interactions. However, time-resolved measurements that directly resolve the phonon dispersion at the nanoscale have not been previously demonstrated. Momentum-resolved vibrational electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) provides access to phonon energies and momenta with nanoscale spatial resolution. Here, we combine momentum-resolved vibrational EELS with pulsed laser heating and synchronised gated electron detection to observe the phonon dispersion of graphite during controlled heating and cooling on the microsecond timescale. Recording both the gain and loss spectra at defined times relative to laser excitation, we determine the temperature at each time delay and follow changes to the phonon branches as a function of temperature. The momentum-resolved spectra reveal a decrease in energy of the optical phonon branch with increasing temperature accompanied by an increase in peak width. These changes are consistent with temperature-dependent phonon renormalisation and scattering associated with anharmonic interactions. The approach is compatible with detector gating on timescales down to 50 ns, providing a route towards extending these measurements to faster dynamics. This work demonstrates time-resolved phonon dispersion spectroscopy using vibrational EELS and provides a route towards probing temperature-dependent phonon dynamics at the nanoscale with simultaneous energy and momentum resolution.

Earthquake-like behavior, in a broad sense, is obtained for $1.5 \leqslant τ 2$

items.title: Direct growth of crystalline spinel GaON films: A wide-bandgap mixed-anion semiconductor
items.summary: Mixed-anion semiconductors offer opportunities for bandgap engineering beyond conventional multication alloys, but competing phases and disorder complicate their synthesis and the identification of their electronic properties. Gallium oxynitride (GaON) could connect the technologically important GaN and Ga2O3 systems, yet establishing a clear relation between its crystal structure, composition and bandgap remains challenging. Here we report the direct growth of crystalline spinel gamma-GaON films by nitrogen-plasma-assisted pulsed-laser deposition. Varying the nitrogen and oxygen supply yields monoclinic beta-Ga2O3, predominantly disordered films and crystalline spinel GaON. Complementary diffraction, atomic-resolution microscopy and elemental analysis establish the spinel structure and nitrogen incorporation. Temperature-dependent photocurrent spectroscopy reveals a clear redshift of the crystalline gamma-GaON response, supporting assignment of a band-edge transition near 4.3 eV at room temperature. These results open opportunities to investigate mixed-anion wide-bandgap semiconductor physics and develop heterostructures.

Here, the authors show that this gyrotropy naturally decomposes into an intrinsic contribution due to interlayer electronic coupling and an extrinsic contribution due to the twisted embedding of the material in physical space. The authors conduct a general symmetry analysis applicable to moiré materials and identify regimes in which the intrinsic, and in which the extrinsic contributions dominate the gyrotropy. Finally, they apply the analysis to twisted bilayer graphene and twisted MoTe 2 .

items.title: Rate-limited nonradiative recombination at a single point defect revealed by time-resolved cathodoluminescence
authors: Thomas F. K. Weatherley, Gunnar Kusch, Jean-François Carlin, Raphaël Butté, Rachel A. Oliver, and Nicolas Grandjean
items.summary: K. Weatherley, Gunnar Kusch, Jean-François Carlin, Raphaël Butté, Rachel A. Oliver, and Nicolas Grandjean Nonradiative point defects in semiconductors are often a major hurdle for efficiency and reliability in optoelectronics, yet directly probing these defects remains difficult. This study uses time-resolved cathodoluminescence mapping plus a diffusion-recombination model to isolate and quantify carrier dynamics at a single point defect in an (In,Ga)N/GaN quantum well. Recombination at the defect is rate-limited by a 16-ps delay, setting a hard bottleneck on defect activity. This insight predicts that defect-related nonradiative recombination saturates at carrier densities routinely reached in LEDs, revealing a fundamental limit not captured by traditional macroscale recombination models.

items.summary: Silicon spin qubits offer a promising platform for scalable quantum processors, but small and highly variable valley splittings can compromise qubit operation across a device. This work uses constrained variational optimization with epitaxial-growth-motivated constraints to design feasible germanium concentration profiles in Si/Si-Ge quantum wells, to enhance deterministic valley splitting while suppressing variability induced by alloy disorder. The principal result is a “modulated wiggle well”, which provides a large, robust, and electrically tunable valley splitting. The approach provides a systematic route for designing reproducible and epitaxially feasible silicon-qubit devices.

Hicken, and Olena Gomonay Antiferromagnets are promising for fast, energy-efficient, high-density memory technologies, but their compensated spins make their domains difficult to image and control optically. The authors use magneto-optical birefringence imaging to show that a Pt capping layer enables ultrafast laser pulses to modify domains in insulating NiO and CoO films. Heiss, M. Trupke, and J. Wrachtrup SiC-based quantum magnetometry is vital for advanced sensing fields because it offers a path to volume-compatible chips, but it is held back because its sensitivity is lower than other platforms like N- V diamond color centers. This study uses a planar 4 H -SiC waveguide platform and wafer-scale fabrication to seamlessly integrate and excite large V2 ensembles. Notably, this streamlined layout achieves a shot-noise limit of 30 nT/√Hz, boosting sensitivity by 2–3 orders of magnitude over that of standard, confocal SiC methods while preserving coherent control.
